freeze_dependencies.where: docs/proposals/03_AUDIO_VIDEO.md §0 R1 (lines 16-31) and §6.2 step 3 (lines 441-444)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The codec-independent stream layout. Every clip occupies exactly [task marker] BEGIN + F placeholders + END, with F = clip_s x fps fixed at compose. AUD.encode writes code ids into the placeholders in place, ONCE, at the freeze. This needs both a fixed fps (so F is known at compose) and a frozen codec (encode once, never again).
freeze_dependencies.why: The layout was chosen so that no window boundary ever moves, which avoids Q-RUN-8. Only the fixed F keeps boundaries still. Freezing the codec adds nothing to that: re-encoding a clip at the same F rewrites the same positions.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: At a fixed fps, keep the placeholders and encode media ids JUST IN TIME when a window is cut, with the codec as it stands; alternatively re-fill in place after each codec refresh. No window moves and Q-RUN-8 is not involved. Cost: spec encode real-time factor 0.0008 on one CPU thread (§6.1, measured), so about 4 ms per 5.12 s window of 25 Hz audio (arithmetic, not measured). An ADAPTIVE fps changes F and therefore the sequence length, so it needs Q-RUN-8 option (a) (splice at the cursor, remap by unit_pos/byte anchor). The other route is an F_max reservation with a learned skip/pad unit.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §0 R3 (lines 37-40), §4.1 lever table (line 260) and startup_refusals (line 272), §6.2 (lines 439-440), §0 run diagram (line 27)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: AUD_FREEZE_AT=3000 (U.Windows) read through an AUD.freeze_at accessor. A startup refusal fires when freeze_at >= planned run windows while a media phase is scheduled, and any media LM phase that starts before the freeze is refused.
freeze_dependencies.why: 'Codec before LM, then freeze' is a stability choice taken from literature that the tree never ran. Per the prior lit research ([S] search extracts), AudioLM, MusicGen, VideoPoet and Chameleon train the tokenizer and then freeze it. No in-tree or prototype run measured a live codec; every prototype LM trained on a corpus encoded once by a frozen codec (design-hybrid/corpus.py:45). The same lit output lists 'Q2 codec drift under continual learning: no source found'.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: The codec trains for the whole run on the AUD_TRAIN_EVERY cadence and never stops. The freeze is replaced by a READINESS Gate: the existing collapse/quiet gauges plus a DATA.recover ceiling, re-read every R row. The startup refusal becomes 'media LM phase before readiness'.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §4.1 entry point freeze(aud, codec, *, clock) (lines 17/277), AUD_VERSION (line 265), §11 aud.version EXACT (lines 631, 638), §6.2 codec drift (line 446), §16 Q11 (line 820)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The freeze Gate hashes the weights into aud.version. A retrain is a NEW version, either held as a second codec for the old block or moved to a new id block with nearest-row init. The rule is 'a codec never changes silently under a trained LM'.
freeze_dependencies.why: Versioning exists so that a change in code meaning can be refused. A live codec changes meaning continuously, so an EXACT version field would refuse every resume.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Replace the freeze with a cadenced AUD.refresh / health Gate. aud.version becomes a reading (the codec step, or a hash at the last refresh) instead of an EXACT geometry field. Codec weights are checkpointed as ordinary trained state. Old-code decodability becomes a MEASURED per-area R-matrix row (codec BWT) instead of a property guaranteed by freezing. Block handover stays available as the arm for a deliberate architecture change.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §0 R13 (line 105) and §5 move #6 (line 331)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: OPT group 'codec' (OPT_CODEC_LR 1e-3) is stepped only before the freeze and retires at it. The freeze stamps the OPT shift that triggers OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM.
freeze_dependencies.why: The group retires only because the codec stops. The shift stamp is tied to media arrival, not to the freeze as such.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: The 'codec' group lives for the whole run under R-OPT (unchanged), with its own schedule and a floor (the OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC precedent). The shift stamp moves to the phase boundary where a media area enters. NOTE: OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM ships at 0 (off), so R13's re-warm is inert unless the lever is set.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §0 R12 (line 97) and §12 cost 'Codec phase ... Only for AUD_FREEZE_AT windows' (line 659)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The cost budget assumes codec training stops at window 3000.
freeze_dependencies.why: This is a cost, not a correctness constraint.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: The cost becomes permanent. R12 measured +16-22% CPU per window with one codec step per window. At AUD_TRAIN_EVERY=4 that is roughly a quarter of that (arithmetic, not measured). It must go into R12's GPU bench arm under MPS with 12 runs per card. An adaptive cadence (train when the reconstruction loss on fresh clips rises) is another option, in the pattern of the SIG floor-skip.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §6.2 (line 445), §6.3 (line 454), §14 (line 727)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: 'The LM loss NEVER back-propagates into the codec'; joint codec+LM backprop is rejected with 'token meaning drifts under the LM'.
freeze_dependencies.why: This is a DIFFERENT question from freezing. A live codec trained only on its own reconstruction/entropy loss is not joint backprop. The rejection evidence is all [S] literature (REPA-E latent collapse, STE codebook collapse, AQM 'old codes must stay decodable'); none of it was measured in the tree or the prototypes. REPA-E and STE are about LM gradients flowing INTO a tokenizer. AQM is about drift, and drift also happens under a live codec with no LM gradient.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Default candidate: a live codec on its own loss, stop-gradient from the LM. Build joint arms behind levers, each watched by the collapse gauges: gradient through codebook embeddings (ETT [S]) or an alignment term (REPA-E [S]).

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §3.1 (line 219) 'Everything persisted stores ABSOLUTE ids', §3.1 module indices (line 211), §16 Q11
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: Persisted absolute code ids (DOM histograms, eval samples, checkpoints, later MEM entries, LM media rows) keep their meaning only if the codec is frozen.
freeze_dependencies.why: Text ids never change meaning: id2bytes is append-only (tok/api.py:1320 docstring; archive remap_mem_ctx). Codec ids WOULD change meaning under a live codec. That is the real cost of going live. What is ABSOLUTELY necessary is narrower: within one training window, the code ids and the LM rows must refer to the same codec state. Just-in-time encoding satisfies that. The address scheme (MEDIA_ID_BASE, block k) is a software convention and can stay.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: (a) FSQ codes are lattice points, so LM media rows can be built compositionally from the lattice coordinates plus a learned residual. This is the LM_COMPOSE analogue (lm/levers.py compose: 'each token's vector from its bytes plus a learned residual'), and it lets row meaning follow the codec's lattice. (b) A code-stability/anchor loss on the codec over a replay set, the analogue of LM.anchor_term (lm/api.py:908). (c) Persist clip REFERENCES rather than codes (a synthetic clip regenerates from its seed) and re-encode on a cadence, the MEM/DOM rekey pattern.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §5 wires (line 383) LM.d_aud_rows <- AUD.levels; derive.media_rows (§0 R14)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The LM media row count is fixed at build as prod(levels)+2 through a wire, and wires are resolved once at build.
freeze_dependencies.why: A fixed row ALLOCATION is necessary because it is a tensor extent. A fixed CODEBOOK is not.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Preallocate media slots with a live count, the pattern LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=4096 (MAY_WIDEN) plus vocab.size() already uses. Levels become MAY_WIDEN. New codes get LM.on_mint-style row initialisation (measured for text: 2.1699 random vs 1.4822 last_first post-mint loss, lm/levers.py via loop.py:2191-2206).

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §4.1 AUD_HOP 160 / AUD_STRIDE 2 (lines 252-253), §0 R8 DATA_AUD_SR 8000, §16 Q2
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The frame rate is hand-set: sr/(hop*stride) = 25 Hz, fixed for the run.
freeze_dependencies.why: 25 Hz was picked from toy CPU prototypes, one seed. §16 Q2 itself records that the 25 Hz LM advantage was measured with a 109-code SEANet codec, not the 559-code spectral codec.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: (i) At minimum, a measured per-run choice (the S3 b / S4 a GPU arms). (ii) An adaptive rate: a multi-rate codec, or variable-rate tokens per clip. One example is minting merges over code sequences with a per-modality online BPE; TOK already has the mint machinery, though the §14 rejection covered only sharing the TEXT table. Every adaptive route changes F and needs Q-RUN-8 (a).

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal Appendix A derive.frames_per_second (lines 861, 907-911) and §3.2 conversions (lines 227-229)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: frames_per_second refuses a non-integer rate (8000,150,1 -> refuses 53.33). media_seconds_per_window and windows_per_media_second assume one fps per modality.
freeze_dependencies.why: The integer-fps refusal protects the exactness of F. It does not protect learning.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: A media unit_pos coordinate in SAMPLES or seconds (the byte_pos analogue), per-clip rate readings, and conversions that take the rate of the clip in hand.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §7 DATA_MEDIA_CLIP_S 1.0 (line 498); §0 R9 clip length per family 'so F is exact' (lines 58-59)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: Fixed-length clips per family make F exact.
freeze_dependencies.why: This is a convenience of synthetic data. Real audio has variable length.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Variable-length clips, with F computed per clip at the current rate.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §8 media generation (line 532)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The sampler draws exactly F = clip_s x fps codes. The mode_fn grammar masks END until F codes, then forces END.
freeze_dependencies.why: This depends on both a fixed fps and fixed clip lengths.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: END is predicted, with a max-length guard from the clip-length prior. The grammar enforces only the modality mask.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §10 WORLD.media_terms (lines 600-601); §3 diagram (line 189)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The media head predicts the FROZEN codec's 64-d latents. §10 says: 'no VICReg on this path: the target is frozen and cannot collapse'. Horizons '1,5' are in FRAMES (40/200 ms only at 25 Hz).
freeze_dependencies.why: The tree's own WORLD already trains against a LIVE target. z_next comes from the same encoder over an UNDETACHED LM.embed (world/api.py:437-468, 149), with VICReg on. Its recorded failure mode is collapse: folding collapse_w to 0.1 gave latent std 0.24, and splitting it back gave 0.97 (world/api.py:429-434).
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Predict the live codec latents with a stop-gradient on the codec side (or an EMA copy of the codec encoder as the target, the BYOL/JEPA shape). Keep the VICReg term on. Declare horizons in milliseconds and convert them through derive at the current rate.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §11 geometry (lines 631-638), §13 S3 'levels change refused'
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: aud.enabled/arch/sr/hop/stride/levels/d/version are all EXACT: 'Changing levels, hop, stride, sr, arch or version ... is refused: it is a new token space'; 'The codec's frozen weights are saved, so old codes stay decodable (AQM)'.
freeze_dependencies.why: EXACT is needed ONLY where a tensor shape depends on the field (d, hid, arch, the NUMBER of FSQ dims) for the weights to load. version, hop, sr and the per-dim level counts do not all set shapes. Their EXACT rule protects code MEANING, which a live codec gives up by design.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: EXACT on shape fields only. Levels MAY_WIDEN. version is a reading. hop/stride become bounds under an adaptive rate. Decodability of old codes is measured per area.

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §9 R matrix (lines 583-591) and §8 grounding table (line 290)
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: bits/code and bits/s (= fps x bits/code) are read per area across phase boundaries as if the unit were stable.
freeze_dependencies.why: bits/code is a CODEC-DEPENDENT unit. Under a live codec (or a changing rate) two R rows measure different alphabets. A live codec can also FORGET old areas, which is the AQM concern.
freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Make the primary readings codec-invariant: DATA.recover exact on decoded audio, mel distance, grounding bits per clip. Keep bits/code tagged with the codec step. Add a per-area codec-reconstruction row (codec BWT). Rehearse the codec: DATA.media_batch draws from every media area seen so far, and synthetic replay costs 0.4-1.3 ms per clip (§7, measured).

freeze_dependencies.where: proposal §5 SIG 'typed' (lines 107-111); tree src/spine/compose.py:2803-2816 (_signature_width, derive-and-keep); src/domains/api.py:311 reservoir, :887 rekey
freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: The signature unit for media is one code. The width is fixed at build from the measured bytes_per_token. DOM reservoirs keep windows in SIG's alphabet, so under 'typed' they keep CODE IDS.

freeze_dependencies.live_alternative: Reservoirs keep clip refs or offsets and are re-encoded at rekey. Media domains decay on each codec refresh, the DOM_TOKC_DECAY analogue.

freeze_dependencies.what_depends_on_freeze_or_fixed_rate: Per-modality loss baselines assume a stationary code alphabet.

q_run_8.current_mechanics: RunClock (src/train/api.py:555) holds windows_in_epoch and a private _in_epoch. advance() (:665) increments step, _in_epoch and batch_len, decides flush_due, then evaluates `rolled = self._in_epoch >= self.windows_in_epoch` (:704). On a roll, epoch+1, _in_epoch=0, the partial batch goes into dropped_windows, and windows_in_epoch is re-armed to None (:715). begin_epoch(n) (:619) is the ONLY setter of windows_in_epoch, and it ZEROES _in_epoch (:663: 'the only quantity a roll may zero'). compose calls it once at stage epoch0 (compose.py:2584) with _windows_in_epoch(sysm) = max(1, (len(Segmentation.ids)-1)//LM.ctx) (compose.py:2982). The loop keeps its own epoch-local cut index win_in_epoch (loop.py:685) and cuts windows from the local `ids = sysm.segmentation.ids` via _window_bounds(ids, i, ctx). TOK.on_window raises Due.retok on TOK_RETOK_EVERY (3000 windows by default). The root ORs Dues per key across the batch (loop.py:991-1003), and _flush consumes the Due: due.retok ONLY does `sysm.retok_pending += 1` and `tok.retok_deferred += 1` (loop.py:2208-2230). The act happens only at an epoch roll (loop.py:~1150-1300): draw_stream, TOK.tokenize of the whole stream at the current vocabulary (:1186), begin_epoch (:1198), shift stamps shift_at_windows/shift_at_steps (:1211, :1219; FAB cooldown and OPT re-warm), resegment = new Segmentation handed to MEM.maintain on the next flush (:1225), DOM.on_retokenize only if vocab.rev moved, then retok_satisfied_by_roll += retok_pending and retok_pending = 0 (:1273). Tick requires `finished` to be tested before `rolled`, so at RUN_EPOCHS=1 the only roll is the finishing one, and every retok ends up in tok.due_dropped at the end (loop.py:1332-1343). The end-of-run warning says every mint is stranded (:1364-1372). Resume: payload['RUN']['clock'] carries in_epoch and windows_in_epoch (loop.py:443-445). compose re-segments the stream at the SAVED vocabulary and REPLAYS the epoch from window 0 with a warning (Q-RUN-10, compose.py:2606-2660). The contract records that a mid-epoch resume therefore feeds TOK.on_window different ids from the uninterrupted run, and says this 'closes when DATA and the loop restore the stream position (the byte-cursor remap, Q-RUN-8 option (a))' (docs/04_CONTRACT.md:4430-4443, 4855-4862). The mechanism (a) needs already exists on the frozen surface: TOK.tokenize(..., start=b) 'segments only the unconsumed tail: minting is append-only, so an already-emitted prefix keeps its meaning' (tok/api.py:1320), and it returns ABSOLUTE byte_pos (_segment, tok/api.py:1264). The archive did exactly this: tail-only retok, `stream = stream[:i] + _ti`, with the cursor kept (self_organize.py:7752-7761).
q_run_8.what_option_a_needs: 1) RUN: a new entry point RunClock.revise_epoch_length(n) (§7 frozen set 137 -> 138; K1/K6 need a LOOP_ORDER row; K13 prose restatements move). It sets windows_in_epoch=n, keeps _in_epoch, refuses a Clock (same as begin_epoch), and refuses n < _in_epoch. It must define n == _in_epoch, where the tail holds no full window: that should roll at the next advance without cutting an empty window, or else the Q-RUN-12 'segmentation ran out' warning path fires. New counter epoch_revisions, published in counters(). 2) LOOP (spine/loop.py): the act moves out of _flush (:2208) into `run` right after _flush returns. By then the batch has been drained (batch/sigs/dids/samples are reset at ~:1082), so no accumulated bound spans two segmentations at any OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS. Splice at k0 = win_in_epoch*ctx: b0 = segmentation.byte_pos[k0]; tail = TOK.tokenize(tok, vocab, stream.bytes, stream.labels, start=b0, regularize=True); new ids = ids[:k0] + tail.ids (and the same for byte_pos and labels). q_run_8.risks: (1) ARCHIVE EVIDENCE AGAINST RETOK SIDE EFFECTS. 23 retoks, 22 of them no-ops, cost 2.189 b/B held-out (4.364 vs 2.175) and 68 points of real-word rate (self_organize.py:7712-7722). The archive attributed this to side effects (lookahead queue flush, held-out cache drop, fabric-growth blackout), not to re-segmentation. The tree refuses no-op retoks (tok.retok_noop) and applies the side effects only when the table moved. The effect of a REAL mid-epoch retok has never been measured in the tree. (2) Minted head rows are trained as softmax negatives for up to TOK_RETOK_EVERY windows before first use, so the post-retok loss spike may exceed the measured 1.4822 immediate-use figure (unmeasured). (3) MEM stale contexts (archive: 82.3% after one growth step) unless a root-passed remap is added. (4) OPT under-anneal: the one in-tree reading shows re-segmenting at vocab 518 shortened 13,429 -> 13,202 ids (-1.7%, a three-epoch small run, loop.py comment near :1344); the owner-scale shrink is unmeasured. (5) A loss-level discontinuity at each act (longer tokens carry more nats/token). This hits FAB regression growth, the MEM per-token surprise gate at a fixed 0.3, DOM competence, the CAP stall test and run.py's loss curve, unless a shift stamp is made and curves are read per byte. (6) Resume determinism: the spliced segmentation is path-dependent (prefix cut under older vocabularies). A resume needs only the tail, so without the byte cursor the Q-RUN-10 epoch replay stays. (7) With TOK_DROPOUT>0, each act's tail draws continue the dropout stream, so run length is a draw (already declared, tok/api.py:1370-1380). (8) An act on the last window of an epoch gives a tail shorter than one window (edge case in revise). (9) Throughput: whole-stream retok taxed the archive x0.77 at 10 MB and x0.25 at 100 MB per RETOK_EVERY (self_organize.py:7752-7755), so tail-only is mandatory. (10) Every default run changes past window 3000, and the defaults table and test fixtures must say so. (11) For MEDIA: the same splice generalises to an adaptive frame rate (F changes for unconsumed clips, remap by unit_pos). A live codec at a FIXED rate does not need it at all.

OPTIONAL halves, each separable: OPT.revise_horizon (about 60-100 lines, +1 entry point); MEM ctx remap through a root-passed function (about 60-100 lines, a MEM.maintain signature move or a declared RetokEvent field); byte-cursor resume (about 80-150 lines, possibly +1 via new_clock(resume_in_epoch=)). Plus the owed measurement: paired seeds of TOK_RETOK_EVERY {0, 3000, 1000} at RUN_EPOCHS=1 on held-out bits/byte, which Q-RUN-8 says must be taken before the ruling.

id_meaning_persistence: TOK Vocabulary: id2bytes (append-only, so a TEXT id's meaning never changes), seq2id match table, merges, retired set, rev; pair TALLY keyed by adjacent id pairs; mint birth steps and probation books. Checkpointed via vocab_state and the save_vocabulary file (tok/api.py:2653, 2829-2912). A retok changes WHICH ids appear for given bytes, never what an id means.

LM rows: emb.weight / head.weight / head.bias indexed by id up to LM_VOCAB_SLOTS (lm/api.py), on_mint row init from parents (:1020), compose residuals and anchor born-steps (:908). The proposal's emb_media[k] / head_media[k] rows are indexed by code. Under a live codec, a code row's learned meaning drifts away from what the code now denotes.
OPT AdamW moments: exp_avg / exp_avg_sq per embedding and head row, id-indexed and checkpointed (OPT state_dict). They carry the gradient history of an id's old meaning.

System.token_seen: (vocab_slots,) appearance counts (loop.py:1853), checkpointed under payload['LOOP'] (loop.py:429) and restored as a prefix (compose.py:2541-2555). The proposal adds per-modality block segments. Consumers: LM.anchor_term, TOK.judge_probation.

DOM Partition: tokc per-domain token-id histograms (domains/api.py:319) used by DOM.prior, decayed by DOM_TOKC_DECAY on retok (:1605); reservoir window samples in SIG's alphabet (bytes by default, token ids at SIG_SPACE=tokens, CODE ids under the proposed 'typed') (:311); centroids and radii in SIG's signature space, refreshed by DOM.rekey (:887); comp books keyed by domain id. All in the DOM state_dict.

MEM store (memory/api.py:190-200): tok = the next-token id, ctx = MEM_KEY_WIN preceding ids, keys = live-LM encodings at write/rekey time, pos = byte offsets (segmentation-invariant), src = DOM domain id, own = FAB owner block. On resegment, ctx/tok are NOT remapped (:1953). The proposal keeps MEM text-only; its MEM-over-media arm would store code ids.

SIG: encoder embedding rows sized 256 (bytes) or vocab_slots (tokens) (compose.py:2819), with the minted-row warm copy via LM.on_mint(sig_emb=). The signature width is fixed at build from bytes_per_token (compose.py:2803). The proposal's 'typed' alphabet is 256 plus media rows.

FAB: expert centroids in the signature space (EMA toward served signatures, FAB_CENT_EMA), per-domain books keyed by DOM ids, competence and error EMAs on the loss level. These carry no token ids, but their numbers are denominated in per-token loss and signature meaning.
WORLD: encoder and predictors over LM.embed rows (obs_emb). Fitness and mass books. The proposed media head would sit over codec latents, whose meaning is tied to the codec state.

EVAL (bodies are stubs): held-out probes are specified in BYTE coordinates and re-tokenized at probe time (eval/api.py:271-330), so they are segmentation-invariant by design. The proposal's grounding prompts ([a2t] [BEGIN] codes [END]) and generated samples stored as codes would carry code meaning; they should store clips/params and re-encode.

R-matrix / readings: text bits/byte is segmentation-invariant. bits/code and bits/s (= fps x bits/code) are CODEC- and RATE-dependent units. The codec ceiling and aud.codes_used gauges read the codec as it was at read time.

CKPT: the whole payload (LM, SIG, FAB, WORLD, MEM, DOM, CAP, OPT, DATA, TOK, LOOP, RUN; loop.py:410-446), the geometry manifest, and the vocabulary file under the same suffix. The proposal adds aud/vid/world_media payload keys and aud.version EXACT.

RUN: payload['RUN']['clock'] in_epoch / windows_in_epoch are window counts under the current segmentation (loop.py:443-445). Cadences.state holds fired steps in Windows. DATA stream_state per-area byte cursors and holdout offsets are segmentation-invariant (data/api.py:1635-1678).

DOM.note_competence / FAB competence / FAB grow_check EMAs / CAP stall band / MEM gate_theta: persisted running statistics of the PER-TOKEN (or per-code) loss or surprise level. They are invalidated in level, not in identity, when segmentation or the codec alphabet changes.

# Map: what "nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" touches

Tree a249595, branch rm-predict-DC. **Nothing below comes from a new experiment.** Every number is either a tree or archive record (the source is cited) or arithmetic (labelled). Notes are in `scratchpad/mm2/map/notes.txt`.

**Scope.** Frozen Configs, frozen §7 signatures (137 entry points), frozen record dataclasses, once-resolved wires, `frozen_rng` and the fixed held-out sets are *software and measurement contracts*. They stay. This map lists **learned things that stop learning**, and **representation rates or sizes fixed by hand**.

## Headline findings
1. **A live codec at a FIXED frame rate does not need Q-RUN-8.**
   - Proposal 03's placeholder layout (§0 R1) keeps window boundaries still because F = clip_s × fps is fixed. Freezing the codec adds nothing to that.
   - Codes can be encoded **just in time when a window is cut**, or re-filled in place after each codec refresh.
   - Cost: spec encode real-time factor 0.0008 (§6.1, measured), about 4 ms per 5.12 s window (arithmetic).
   - Only an **adaptive frame rate** changes F, hence the sequence length. That, and only that, needs Q-RUN-8 option (a).
2. **The freeze was never measured in the tree.**
   - The case for it is literature search extracts ([S]): REPA-E, STE collapse, AQM, and "every surveyed system froze".
   - The prior literature pass itself records "codec drift under CL: no source found".
   - Every prototype LM trained on a corpus that a frozen codec encoded once.
   - "No LM gradient into the codec" is a separate question from "the codec stops training". A codec trained only on its own loss is not joint backprop.
3. **The real cost of a live codec is meaning drift of persisted code ids.** Text ids never change meaning, because `id2bytes` is append-only; a retok changes the segmentation only. Code ids would change meaning. The consumers that inherit the drift:
   - LM media rows and their AdamW moments
   - `token_seen`
   - DOM reservoirs and histograms
   - MEM (if media is ever stored)
   - WORLD media targets
   - eval prompts held as codes
   - bits/code readings in the R matrix
4. **The tree already has the patterns a live codec needs.**
   - SIG trains in the loop, while DOM reservoirs are re-encoded by `DOM.rekey` and FAB centroids track by EMA.
   - MEM keys come from the live LM and are re-encoded every 200 windows.
   - **WORLD already trains against a LIVE, undetached target with VICReg** (world/api.py:437-468). §10's "no VICReg because the target is frozen" is the exception, not the rule.
   - Minting plus `LM.on_mint` row init, with `LM_COMPOSE`/`anchor_term` as the handover.
   - Self-inflicted-shift stamps: FAB cooldown and `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM`.
   - Schedules with non-zero floors: `OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC` 0.05, `FAB_BAL_FLOOR` 0.15.
5. **The biggest learned thing frozen tree-wide is TEXT segmentation.**
   - At `RUN_EPOCHS=1` every retok is deferred to a roll that never comes (loop.py:2208-2230, 1332-1343).
   - About 600 mints per 20k-window run are stranded (arithmetic from `TOK_GROW_EVERY` 200 × burst 6).
   - Their head rows sit in the softmax as negatives until first use (inferred; size unmeasured).
   - Contract, measured 2026-09-24: `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` changes nothing at any `RUN_EPOCHS` (bit-identical 418-flush curve at 0 and 10).

## 1. Proposal 03 dependencies on a frozen codec or fixed rate (20 mapped; none absolutely necessary)
- **Freeze machinery:**
  - `AUD_FREEZE_AT` 3000, its accessor, and the startup refusals (R3, §4.1, §6.2)
  - `freeze()` Gate with the weight hash into `aud.version` (EXACT)
  - OPT `'codec'` group retiring at the freeze (R13)
  - cost budget "only for AUD_FREEZE_AT windows" (§12)
  - `AUD.encode` at the roll, and the `aud.freeze` row (§5)
  - VID equivalents (§4.2)
- **Meaning-stability assumptions:**
  - "persist ABSOLUTE ids", "frozen ids must never change meaning" (§3.1, Q11)
  - `LM.d_aud_rows` wire fixing the codebook size
  - `aud.levels/hop/stride/sr/version` EXACT (§11)
  - bits/code as the R-matrix unit
  - `WORLD.media_terms` over frozen latents with no VICReg (§10)
  - per-modality loss baselines (R11)
- **Fixed-rate assumptions:**
  - `AUD_HOP`/`AUD_STRIDE` giving 25 Hz
  - `derive.frames_per_second` refusing a non-integer rate
  - `DATA_MEDIA_CLIP_S` and per-family exact F (R9)
  - generation forcing END after exactly F codes (§8)
  - WORLD horizons in frames
  - media windows per phase as a startup reading (R4)
  - SIG `'typed'` width in codes
  - Griffin-Lim, which is fixed but not learned
- **What is absolutely necessary:** within one training window, the codes and the LM rows must come from the same codec state (just-in-time encoding satisfies this), and EXACT geometry only where a tensor shape depends on the field.
- **Live alternatives (details in `freeze_dependencies`):**
  - a readiness Gate instead of a freeze
  - a permanent `'codec'` group with a floor
  - just-in-time or refresh encoding
  - compositional LM media rows from FSQ lattice coordinates (the `LM_COMPOSE` analogue)
  - a code-stability/anchor loss and codec rehearsal (synthetic replay is 0.4-1.3 ms per clip)
  - a live WORLD target with VICReg or an EMA target, horizons in ms
  - predicted END
  - media slots preallocated and MAY_WIDEN
  - codec-invariant primary readings (`DATA.recover` exact, mel, grounding bits) plus a per-area codec BWT row

## 2. Other learned or fixed things tree-wide (defaults stated)
- **Frozen in effect:**
  - segmentation, and minted tokens stranded
  - `world_proj` held at zero by `WORLD_FEEDBACK`=False
  - the SIG signature width, fixed from build-time bytes_per_token
  - the OPT horizon, fixed at build (Q-OPT-5)
- **Arms, off by default:** `TOK_FREEZE_AT` (0 = never), `TOK_MODE` fixed/bytes, `SIG_MODE=bigram`, `MEM_KEY_SRC=frozen` (not built), `FAB_GROW=0`, `DOM_MANAGE=0`.
- **Fixed capacity:**
  - `CAP_TARGETS` off; `CAP_PIN_WINDOWS` 20000 cannot fire in a 20k run
  - `LM_VOCAB_SLOTS` 4096, `FAB_SLOTS` 4096, `WORLD_NMAX` 6
- **Fixed structure:** EXACT widths (`LM_WIDTH` 128, `LM_CTX` 128, `SIG_D` 64, `WORLD_LAT` 32, `FAB_RANK` 8). Necessary as built, because checkpoints load by tensor shape.
- **Units that shift under an adaptive rate:** position-denominated horizons (`WORLD_HORIZON` 1 token, `MEM_KEY_WIN` 8, ctx 128) change meaning in seconds.
- **Hand-set thresholds with adaptive arms:** `DOM_SHIFT_RULE` constant, `MEM_WRITE_MODE` fixed.
- **Relevant defaults:**
  - TOK: `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 3000, `TOK_GROW_EVERY` 200
  - LM: `LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS` False, `LM_NEW_ROW_INIT` mean, `LM_COMPOSE` False
  - OPT: `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM` **0 (off)**, `OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC` 0.05
  - DOM: `DOM_TOKC_DECAY` 0.5
  - `MEM_REKEY_EVERY` 200, `SIG_SPACE` bytes, `WORLD_FEEDBACK` False, `RUN_EPOCHS` 1

## 3. Q-RUN-8 option (a): "revise the epoch length and keep the cursor"
- **Why it is blocked today.** `begin_epoch` is the only setter of `windows_in_epoch`, and it zeroes `_in_epoch`.
- **The splice already has what it needs.** `TOK.tokenize(start=byte)` already segments only the tail with absolute `byte_pos`, and the archive did exactly this splice.
- **Needs:**
  1. `RunClock.revise_epoch_length(n)` (+1 entry point, 137 -> 138).
  2. The act moves from `_flush` to `run` after the flush, when the batch is empty:
     - splice `ids[:k0] + tail`, re-resolve `sig_stream`, revise the length;
     - resegment to MEM, `on_retokenize` to DOM;
     - a shift stamp;
     - redefined `tok.retok_*` counters.
  3. A decision on OPT horizon revision; the under-anneal is otherwise inside one epoch.
  4. A MEM context remap passed in by the root, since MEM cannot import TOK. Archive: 82.3% of stored contexts go stale after one growth step.
  5. Optionally, a byte-cursor resume, which also closes the Q-RUN-10 replay.
  6. Rewriting tests/test_tok_dom_cap.py T1/D1.
- **Size:** about 350-500 lines core, about 550-850 lines with all halves; 1-3 frozen-surface moves.
- **Risk to take seriously:** the archive measured 2.189 b/B lost to 23 retoks, 22 of them no-ops, and attributed it to side effects. The tree now refuses no-ops. A real mid-epoch retok has never been measured in the tree.
- **Default change:** because `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` ships at 3000, (a) changes every default run past window 3000.
- **Owed measurement:** paired seeds of `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` {0, 3000, 1000} at `RUN_EPOCHS=1`, on held-out bits/byte.

## 4. Persisted id meaning
Covered in `id_meaning_persistence`:
- TOK tally and vocabulary
- LM rows and AdamW moments
- `token_seen`
- DOM `tokc`, reservoir and centroids
- MEM tok/ctx/keys
- SIG rows and width
- FAB and WORLD loss-level books
- EVAL prompts (byte-coordinate by design)
- R-matrix units
- CKPT payload
- RUN in-epoch position

Text survives a retok by construction; code ids would not survive a live codec.

findings.claim: REPA-E does NOT back-propagate the generative (diffusion) loss into the VAE. The official training loop computes the SiT loss on z.detach(); the VAE is updated by its own losses (L1 reconstruction, LPIPS, KL, GAN) plus the REPA alignment loss routed through the SiT, whose weights are frozen for that pass. The README says joint training with the standard diffusion loss is observed to be ineffective, often degrading final performance.
findings.source: arXiv 2504.10483 (ICCV 2025); code github.com/End2End-Diffusion/REPA-E, train_repae.py lines ~355-440, and README
findings.numbers: README: 17x speedup over REPA and 45x over vanilla. SiT-XL/2 with SD-VAE init, 80 epochs: gFID 4.07 (1.67 with CFG). On a frozen SD-VAE: SiT at 1400 epochs 8.30, REPA at 800 epochs 5.84. E2E-VA-VAE + REPA, 800 epochs: 1.69 (1.12 with CFG).
findings.relevance: The main paper that 6.3 cites against joint training actually shows a live tokenizer trained jointly and working. The conditions: the generator's likelihood loss is stopped at the tokenizer, and the tokenizer keeps its own reconstruction objective.

findings.claim: REPA-E project page: VAE and diffusion model trained jointly from scratch, with no VAE pre-training, reach gFID 4.34 at 400K iterations (80 epochs). REPA on a frozen SD-VAE reaches 7.90; with VAE init, REPA-E reaches 4.07. At 40 epochs: scratch 7.54, VAE init 7.17, REPA 11.10.
findings.numbers: gFID 4.34 scratch / 4.07 init / 7.90 REPA frozen-VAE at 80 epochs; 7.54 / 7.17 / 11.10 at 40 epochs
findings.relevance: Direct evidence that a codec that was never pretrained, trained alongside its generator, can beat a frozen codec under the stop-grad plus own-loss recipe. Caveat: the alignment target (DINOv2) is a frozen pretrained model, which this project does not have.

findings.topic: joint codec+generator training: mechanism of latent collapse
findings.claim: When the diffusion loss is back-propagated into the VAE, it pushes toward a simpler latent with lower spatial variance. That is easier to denoise but degrades generation. The paper tabulates latent variance for (1) a frozen VAE, (2) naive end-to-end with diffusion loss, and (3) end-to-end with REPA loss.
findings.source: arXiv 2504.10483 (search extracts of the arXiv/CVF pages and the ICCV supplemental); the exact table values were not read
findings.relevance: Defines the precise collapse condition: the generator's own loss reaching the tokenizer. That is narrower than 'joint training'.

findings.topic: joint VQ tokenizer + AR LM training (STE collapse)
findings.claim: GEAR: sending the next-token-prediction gradient into a VQ tokenizer through the straight-through estimator collapses (gFID about 105). The fix is a dual read-out. A hard one-hot branch trains the AR with NTP. A differentiable soft branch, softmax(-d/tau), carries an alignment loss that updates only the tokenizer. The NTP loss never touches the tokenizer. The tokenizer loss is the standard VQ objective (reconstruction + LPIPS + GAN + entropy + commitment) plus the soft alignment term. The tokenizer ends up lower-entropy and less DINOv2-like, with reconstruction preserved.
findings.numbers: STE end-to-end: gFID about 105. GEAR: about 10x faster ImageNet gFID convergence than LlamaGen-REPA. T2I: a fresh AR on the tuned tokenizer reaches the baseline's NTP loss 2.5x faster and its REPA loss 11.1x faster. Works across VQ, LFQ and IBQ.
findings.relevance: The closest published analogue to discrete codes in an LM. The STE collapse that 6.3 cites is real, and a published remedy keeps the tokenizer co-trained. GEAR then freezes the tuned tokenizer for downstream reuse, so never-frozen deployment is not demonstrated.

findings.topic: joint VQ tokenizer + AR LM training (why collapse happens)
findings.claim: NTP rewards a token stream that is easy to predict. A tokenizer can supply one trivially by driving its index distribution to low entropy and emitting a few dominant codes, while faithful reconstruction needs a high-entropy, fully used codebook. When the prediction loss reaches the tokenizer, prediction wins. EOSTok reports the same STE collapse. Its fix is an Autoregressive Prediction Reconstruction (APR) loss: the AR's teacher-forced predictions are decoded to pixels and reconstructed, so predictions must carry content. The 1D tokenizer and the AR are trained simultaneously from scratch.
findings.source: GEAR arXiv 2606.32039 (search extract of its text); EOSTok arXiv 2605.00503 (ICML 2026, search extract)
findings.relevance: The mechanism shows why the tree's entropy bonus and collapse gauge are the right counterweights. APR is a remedy that needs no external pretrained model.

findings.topic: entropy preservation in end-to-end latent models
findings.claim: GenFirst: direct end-to-end training is prone to latent collapse and to a generation-reconstruction conflict. The entropy term of the KL objective is essential against collapse, because reconstruction and prior fitting both shrink the posterior. Their schedule lets the generative objective shape the latent first, under weak reconstruction pressure and explicit entropy preservation, and then strengthens reconstruction.
findings.numbers: SiT gFID 0.97 with CFG, 1.45 without, ImageNet-256; MMDiT GenEval 0.90
findings.relevance: The generator loss can reach the tokenizer directly if entropy is explicitly preserved. The published remedy is the same kind of term as the tree's AUD_ENT_W.

findings.claim: Diffusion as Self-Distillation (DSD): naive joint training of encoder, decoder and diffusion in one network fails through latent collapse. It is stabilised with stop-gradient and EMA targets borrowed from self-distillation methods.
findings.relevance: A no-pretrained-model remedy (EMA plus stop-grad), which fits the owner's from-scratch constraint better than REPA-style alignment to DINOv2.

findings.topic: tokenizer co-trained with an AR prior
findings.claim: LARP integrates a lightweight AR transformer during video-tokenizer training, so the latent space is shaped for both reconstruction and AR generation. The prior's NLL is added to the reconstruction loss and optimises both the prior and the tokenizer; the prior improves generation FVD across token counts.
findings.source: arXiv 2410.21264 (ICLR 2025 oral); README github.com/hywang66/LARP (verified: AR prior integrated during training); the loss details come from search extracts
findings.numbers: README: LARP-L-Long tokenizer 173M params, reconstruction FVD 20; AR 632M, generation FVD 57; frame prediction FVD 5.1
findings.relevance: A co-trained AR prior that shapes the codec without collapse. The LM-side analogue: a small prior inside the codec phase rather than the full LM gradient.

findings.claim: CRT uses knowledge of the stage-2 AR model to regularise stage-1 tokenizer latents. Tokens become easier to model at the same compression rate: tokenization that is worse for reconstruction can be better for generation.
findings.numbers: 2-3x compute efficiency; matches LlamaGen-3B (2.18 FID) with 256 vs 576 tokens per image and 775M vs 3.1B params
findings.relevance: Supports letting LM-side predictability shape the codec through a bounded regulariser rather than through NTP backprop.

findings.topic: live tokenizer under an AR model (world models)
findings.claim: IRIS keeps training its discrete autoencoder for the whole run while the AR transformer trains on its tokens. The tokenizer trains every epoch from epoch 6, the world model from epoch 26 and the actor-critic from epoch 51, over 600 epochs of 200 steps each. The world-model loss encodes raw observations with the CURRENT tokenizer under torch.no_grad on every batch, so tokens are never stored stale and the AR loss never reaches the tokenizer.
findings.source: arXiv 2209.00588 (ICLR 2023); code github.com/eloialonso/iris, config/trainer.yaml and src/models/world_model.py line ~99
findings.numbers: config: tokenizer start_after_epochs 5, world_model 25, actor_critic 50, epochs 600, steps_per_epoch 200. Search extract: Atari 100k mean human-normalised score 1.046, superhuman on 10 of 26 games.
findings.relevance: The cleanest precedent for the owner's wish: a never-frozen codec, a stop-gradient LM, and codes recomputed from raw data at read time.

findings.topic: live categorical encoder jointly trained with a predictor
findings.claim: DreamerV3 trains its categorical latent encoder jointly with the sequence model, without stopping the predictor's influence entirely. The KL is split: dyn = KL(sg(post) || prior) at weight 1.0 trains the predictor; rep = KL(post || sg(prior)) at weight 0.1 pulls the encoder toward predictability; both are clipped at free_nats 1.0. Categoricals mix 1% uniform (unimix 0.01), and reconstruction is weight 1.0.
findings.source: code github.com/danijar/dreamerv3, dreamerv3/rssm.py lines 120-129 and configs.yaml line 86-91
findings.numbers: loss_scales rec 1.0, dyn 1.0, rep 0.1; free_nats 1.0; unimix 0.01; default stoch 32 x classes 64
findings.relevance: A tested recipe for letting predictability pressure into a live discrete encoder safely: a down-weighted, floor-clipped term plus a reconstruction anchor.

findings.topic: continual compression; 'old codes must stay decodable'
findings.claim: AQM does not freeze its codec. It freezes only the VQ codebook of a block (codebook EMA decay set to 1, unused codes trimmed) once the running fraction of samples compressed below threshold exceeds 0.90. Encoder and decoder keep training on incoming data plus rehearsal: stored codes are decoded, re-fed through the model, and the decoder is trained to reconstruct them. An EMA decoder (decay 0.99) is kept after the freeze, and drift of stored reconstructions is measured.
findings.source: arXiv 1911.08019 (ICML 2020); code github.com/pclucas14/adaptive-quantization-modules, common/modular.py lines 95-150 and 328-370, gen_main.py lines 110-145, eval.py eval_drift
findings.numbers: freeze trigger avg_comp > 0.90 (code comment: used to be 0.75, then 0.90, then 0.95); ema decoder decay 0.99
findings.relevance: The AQM constraint binds on STORED codes. FSQ's parameter-free lattice already gives the fixed id-to-point map that AQM obtained by freezing a codebook, so the encoder and decoder can stay live with decoder rehearsal.

findings.topic: tokenizer drift under a trained generator (continual)
findings.claim: DACT: in generative recommendation, naively fine-tuning the tokenizer on new data changes the token sequences of most existing items and undermines the generator's learned token-embedding alignment. The remedy has two parts: tokenizer fine-tuning with a jointly trained drift-identification module (different optimisation for drifting and stationary items), and a relaxed-to-strict hierarchical code reassignment that limits unnecessary code changes.
findings.relevance: Published confirmation that 'token meaning drifts under the LM' is a real cost of a live tokenizer, with a published mitigation: bounded reassignment rather than a freeze.

findings.claim: FSQ projects to a few dimensions and rounds each one to a small set of fixed values. The implicit codebook is the product of those sets and has no parameters, and FSQ needs no commitment loss, codebook reseeding, code splitting, entropy penalty or EMA codebook. The authors state that FSQ does not suffer from codebook collapse.
findings.relevance: With FSQ, nothing in the id-to-point map is learned, so there is nothing to freeze there. A live codec's drift is entirely in the encoder (which audio lands on id k) and the decoder (what id k sounds like). Note the tree measured plain FSQ collapsing in 3 of 5 runs, contrary to this claim; see iFSQ.

findings.claim: With equal-interval quantization, vanilla FSQ can suffer activation collapse. iFSQ replaces tanh with 2*sigmoid(1.6x)-1, a distribution-matching activation that uses the bins with equal probability. Their optimum lies at about 4 bits per dimension.
findings.relevance: A codec-internal collapse cause that exists without any LM gradient. It is an argument for gauges and a better activation, not for a freeze.

findings.claim: Trained VQ-VAE representations can live in a 1-2% rank subspace, which sets a loss lower bound that codebook tricks do not pass. The fix is an AE warm-up: train unquantized first, then introduce VQ. Shown on VQGAN and WavTokenizer.
findings.relevance: Another codec-internal failure (no LM involved). For a live codec, a continuous warm-up phase is a published remedy.

findings.claim: MoCo: a slowly progressing momentum key encoder keeps a queue of keys encoded by past encoders consistent. m = 0.999 works much better than m = 0.9, and m = 0 fails.
findings.numbers: default m = 0.999; m = 0.9 markedly worse (exact table values not read)
findings.relevance: The closest published analogue to stored codes that must stay compatible with a changing encoder. The literature's remedy is an EMA encoder, not a frozen one.

findings.claim: V-JEPA's target encoder is a deepcopy of the encoder, updated by EMA under torch.no_grad, with momentum scheduled linearly from 0.998 to 1.0 over training. At the end of the schedule the target is effectively frozen.
findings.relevance: A template for a slow codec that feeds WORLD and the LM. For a never-frozen system the schedule must cap below 1.0.

findings.claim: data2vec's teacher is an EMA of the student with tau ramped from 0.999 to 0.9999. Targets are the averaged, normalised top-K teacher layers; normalisation plus stop-grad on the EMA teacher prevents collapse.
findings.relevance: Moving but slow targets for WORLD.media_terms if the codec latent is live.

findings.claim: HuBERT recomputes its discrete targets between iterations. Iteration 1 uses k-means (100 clusters) on MFCC; iteration 2 uses k-means (500) on layer-6 features of the iteration-1 model. The refined targets have higher phone purity.
findings.source: arXiv 2106.07447 (search extract; the PNMI numbers come from a secondary summary)
findings.numbers: k = 100 on 39-d MFCC, then k = 500 on layer 6; PNMI 0.704 vs 0.243 (secondary source)
findings.relevance: Precedent for a tokenizer that changes at a few scheduled points with the model retrained on the new targets. This is the epoch-roll retok pattern.

findings.claim: BEiT v2 trains its VQ-KD tokenizer (8192 codes, 32-d, L2-normalised lookup against codebook collapse) to reconstruct CLIP-B/16 features, then uses it as a fixed tokenizer for masked image modeling.
findings.relevance: Shows that freezing is the common engineering default, typically with pretrained teachers. It is a convention, not evidence that a live tokenizer fails.

findings.claim: Vocabulary curriculum: pre-training alternates entropy-guided vocabulary expansion with model optimisation, starting from characters. It gives lower BPC than fixed-vocabulary training and a shallower log-vocab vs BPC slope.
findings.relevance: Published evidence that an LM can train through tokenizer changes mid-run when the corpus is re-segmented. That is exactly what Q-RUN-8's RunClock.revise_epoch_length would enable for TOK and for a live codec.

findings.claim: ZeTT trains a hypernetwork that predicts input and output embeddings for any new tokenizer, coming close to the original model's performance. FOCUS initialises new token embeddings as sparsemax-weighted combinations of overlapping tokens, and full vocabulary replacement with FOCUS beat extending the original vocabulary.
findings.source: ZeTT arXiv 2405.07883; FOCUS arXiv 2305.14481 / EMNLP 2023 (search extracts)
findings.relevance: Literature behind LM_NEW_ROW_INIT-style initialisation when a live codec re-maps or mints codes.

findings.claim: GIVT replaces the input lookup table with a linear projection of real-valued vectors and the output softmax with a Gaussian mixture. It models the unquantized latents of a beta-VAE and beats VQ-GAN and MaskGIT.
findings.relevance: If the codec stays continuous, there is no id table to drift. A linear or MLP input over code coordinates is also a way to make discrete FSQ ids drift-tolerant.

findings.claim: MAR (autoregressive image generation without vector quantization) uses a per-token diffusion loss head (DiffLoss MLP) on continuous tokens.
findings.relevance: Removes the discrete bottleneck. The codec's latent can then be the LM target directly, with the same live-codec considerations as REPA-E.

findings.topic: continuous tokens in a mixed text+image LM
findings.claim: Transfusion trains one transformer with next-token loss on text and diffusion on images. It scales significantly better than quantizing images to discrete tokens, and with modality-specific layers an image can be compressed to 16 patches. Its image VAE is pretrained and fixed.
findings.numbers: up to 7B params from scratch; 16 patches per image
findings.relevance: Strongest scaling evidence for continuous over discrete media tokens. It still uses a frozen VAE, so it does not settle the live-codec question.

findings.claim: CALM (Kyutai) models continuous audio-VAE frames autoregressively with a consistency-model head. It argues that standard VAEs are easier to train, avoid codebook collapse, and reconstruct better than RVQ.
findings.numbers: consistency head 12.3x faster than the RQ-Transformer; Pocket TTS 100M runs faster than real time on a laptop CPU
findings.relevance: A CPU-feasible continuous audio LM precedent.

findings.claim: VibeVoice uses continuous acoustic and semantic speech tokenizers at 7.5 Hz with next-token diffusion. The low rate is chosen for efficiency on long sequences, and its ASR accepts up to 60 minutes within 64K tokens.
findings.relevance: A strong recent system chose a very low rate with continuous latents.

findings.topic: frame rate choice of a strong from-scratch-trained codec
findings.claim: Mimi compresses 24 kHz audio to a 12.5 Hz representation at 1.1 kbps, fully streaming, with an 80 ms frame. The stated reason: getting closer to the average frame rate of text tokens (about 3-4 Hz) limits the number of autoregressive steps in Moshi. A WavLM distillation loss makes the first codebook semantic.
findings.numbers: 12.5 Hz, 1.1 kbps, 80 ms latency; compare SpeechTokenizer 50 Hz / 4 kbps and SemantiCodec 50 Hz / 1.3 kbps
findings.relevance: The rationale for the Hz in the best-known speech-text system is to match text token rate and cut AR steps, which applies directly to a shared text+audio LM.

findings.claim: TaDiCodec is a diffusion-autoencoder tokenizer trained end-to-end for quantization and reconstruction, with text guidance in the decoder. It reaches 6.25 Hz at 0.0875 kbps with one codebook for 24 kHz speech.
findings.relevance: Shows how low rates go when the decoder is strong. It depends on text conditioning, which aud/tones lacks.

findings.topic: dynamic frame rate by merging similar frames
findings.claim: FlexiCodec merges adjacent semantically similar frames. A merging_threshold controls the rate: 1.0 gives a standard 12.5 Hz codec, 0.91 about 8.3 Hz, 0.86 about 6.25 Hz. Rate is controllable at inference between about 3 and 12.5 Hz, and outputs carry per-token durations (token_lengths).
findings.relevance: The simplest content-adaptive rate mechanism, a cosine threshold over adjacent latents. It could sit on top of the spec codec's 50 fps latent.

findings.topic: dynamic frame rate in a spoken LM
findings.claim: FlexiSLM is described as the first spoken LM with dynamic, controllable frame rates on input and output. One trained model can be steered between 12.5 Hz and 4.0 Hz without retraining, and matches state-of-the-art 7B models at 6.25 Hz. Search extract: at 6.25 Hz it roughly halves inference time vs 12.5 Hz.
findings.numbers: 12.5 -> 4.0 Hz steerable; 6.25 Hz about half the inference time of 12.5 Hz (search extract)
findings.relevance: Direct LM-side evidence that a variable rate works inside the LM, not only in the codec.

findings.topic: variable frame rate tokenizer with implicit durations
findings.claim: VARSTok segments speech into variable-length units with temporal-aware density-peak clustering. Its implicit duration coding folds content and span into one token index, so no separate duration predictor is needed. The encoder returns discrete codes plus cluster lengths.
findings.source: arXiv 2509.04685 (AAAI 2026 oral); README github.com/FunAudioLLM/FunResearch/tree/main/VARSTok (verified: mechanism, and a known sign bug in the paper's clustering)
findings.numbers: Search extract: up to 23% fewer tokens than a 40 Hz fixed-rate baseline, with better naturalness and lower TTS WER
findings.relevance: One way to keep variable-rate codes inside a single id space: the duration goes into the id.

findings.claim: CodecSlime adds dynamic frame rate to a fixed-rate codec. ScheDFR merges frames by dynamic programming over feature similarity at inference, and Melt-and-Cool post-training adapts the backbone, first to random downsampling schedules and then to the DP schedules.
findings.numbers: at 40 Hz DFR (about 600 bps), reconstruction WER up to 32% lower relative to fixed-rate baselines of the same architecture
findings.relevance: A post-training route to adaptive rate that keeps an existing codec.

findings.claim: TFC (temporally flexible coding) chooses among 75, 37.5 and 18.75 Hz per segment from an entropy-based estimate of information density, with a tunable average rate.
findings.numbers: 37.5 Hz TFC comparable to or better than 75 Hz DAC at 3 kbps
findings.relevance: Rate set by a measured signal rather than by hand.

findings.claim: DyCAST is a variable-frame-rate 16 kHz codec built on FocalCodec, with soft character alignment and explicit duration modelling.
findings.relevance: Needs text alignment, so it does not apply to aud/tones. It shows that explicit duration tokens are a working alternative to implicit duration ids.

findings.topic: learned skip predictor for dynamic rate
findings.claim: Elastic Time is a dynamic frame-rate re-bottleneck with a lightweight causal latent predictor that decides which frames can be skipped and later reconstructed. The repo also ships Conv-Downsample, H-Net and CodecSlime baselines. It is built on a frozen pretrained Stable Audio Open autoencoder.
findings.relevance: Predictability decides the rate: frames the predictor can fill are skipped. The published version relies on a frozen autoencoder.

findings.topic: low-rate quality cliff is partly a training artefact
findings.claim: Probing Low Frame Rate Degradation reproduces a quality cliff at 6.25 Hz and traces it to training on a fixed clip duration, which leaves too few tokens per clip and starves the decoder of inter-token context. Phonemic collisions and codebook saturation are not the cause. With the fix, WER degrades smoothly down to 3.1 Hz and 1.6 Hz.
findings.numbers: cliff at 6.25 Hz removed; smooth degradation to 3.1 and 1.6 Hz
findings.relevance: Our clips are 1 s (25 tokens at 25 Hz, 12-13 at 12.5 Hz), so any rate comparison on 1 s clips may be confounded by this effect.

findings.claim: BPE over discrete audio tokens shortens sequences by 1.6-2.4x, gives 2.8x (5k vocab) to 5.0x (20k vocab) faster AR inference, and improves syntax capture in a speech LM.
findings.relevance: The LM-side merge that mirrors TOK. It would inherit TOK's retok-deferral problem under RUN_EPOCHS = 1.

findings.topic: speech LM scaling and coarse tokens
findings.claim: Cuervo and Marxer: the linguistic performance of speech LMs scales up to three orders of magnitude more slowly than text LMs. BPE-style coarser tokenization of speech units did not improve performance in their study.
findings.relevance: A counterweight to acoustic BPE. Merging units did not help there, while lower-rate units trained as such did (SyllableLM).

findings.claim: SyllableLM ships SylBoost units at 8.33, 6.25 and 5.0 Hz. The paper reports 30x less training compute and a 4x wall-clock inference speedup while matching or beating AudioLM and TWIST.
findings.source: arXiv 2410.04029 (ICLR 2025); README github.com/AlanBaade/SyllableLM (verified: the rates); compute numbers from search extract
findings.relevance: For content that is semantically sparse, a much lower rate helps the LM a lot.

findings.claim: Syllabic tokens at 4-5 Hz match or beat high-frame-rate tokens on SLU benchmarks, with more than 2x less training time and 5x fewer FLOPs.
findings.relevance: More evidence for lower rates on the LM side.

findings.topic: patching speech tokens inside the LM
findings.claim: The Latent Speech-Text Transformer aggregates speech tokens into latent patches as higher-level AR units, aligning the granularity of speech and text. It gains up to +6.5% absolute on speech HellaSwag, the gain grows with scale under compute-controlled training, and patches compactly capture recurring patterns such as silence.
findings.relevance: The rate can be adapted inside the LM (BLT-style patches) while the codec keeps a fine fixed grid.

findings.claim: H-Net's routing module sets boundary probability p_t = clamp((1 - cos(q_t, k_{t-1}))/2, 0, 1) and places a boundary when p_t > 0.5: new chunks start where adjacent representations are dissimilar. A smoothing module interpolates with p. Search extract: a ratio loss steers toward a target compression ratio N; a one-stage byte-level H-Net beats a BPE Transformer when compute- and data-matched.
findings.source: arXiv 2507.07955; code github.com/goombalab/hnet, hnet/modules/dc.py lines 69-165 and configs (vocab_size 256)
findings.numbers: boundary if (1 - cos)/2 > 0.5; the ratio-loss target N is a hyperparameter (search extract)
findings.relevance: End-to-end learned rate, but the average rate is still steered by a target ratio N. It is the same similarity principle as FlexiCodec's merging.

findings.claim: BLT groups bytes into dynamically sized patches by next-byte entropy from a small byte LM (a global threshold, or a relative/monotonic rule), putting more compute where data is complex. The README reports a scaling study up to 8B parameters and 8T training bytes.
findings.numbers: README: up to 8B params, 8T training bytes (a search summary said 4T; the README says 8T). Search extract: matches Llama 3 at equal training FLOPs with up to 50% fewer inference FLOPs.
findings.relevance: In this system, the LM's or WORLD's own surprise could set audio patch boundaries. The threshold remains a knob.

findings.claim: dMel discretizes log mel-filterbank channels into intensity bins with no training: 80 filterbanks, 4 bits per channel, log values clamped to [-7, 2], 12.5 ms stride (80 frames/s) at 16 kHz. The authors report better reconstruction than model-based tokenizers (HuBERT-KM, SpeechTokenizer, EnCodec, Mimi), especially out of domain, and predict all channels of a frame in parallel. Reconstruction to waveform uses a trained vocoder.
findings.source: arXiv 2407.15835; code github.com/apple/dmel (run_example.py, dmel/dmel.py); demo page source github.com/apple/dmel-demo
findings.numbers: 80 channels x 4 bits, 12.5 ms stride, clamp [-7, 2]
findings.relevance: A tokenizer with no learned weights, so nothing to freeze or drift: the audio analogue of bytes, with learned merging (BPE, H-Net, LST) on top. Its fixed binning is 'fixed', which the owner may or may not accept.

findings.claim: FlexTok resamples images into ordered 1D sequences whose token list can be truncated in a nested fashion (README). Search extract: 1-256 tokens via nested dropout with a rectified-flow decoder, FID < 2 across 8-128 tokens on ImageNet.
findings.relevance: The per-sample token count becomes a choice made at encode time, not a fixed F.

findings.topic: adaptive token count, video with FSQ
findings.claim: ElasticTok encodes each frame (or block) into a variable number of tokens by masking a random-length tail during training, conditioned on prior frames. The released config uses an FSQ bottleneck with levels (8,8,8,5,5,5), min 256 and max 4096 tokens, 4 frames per block. Search extract: comparable reconstruction with 2-5x fewer tokens (2.4x at 0.001 MSE, 5x at 0.015 MSE).
findings.relevance: The closest precedent to FSQ plus a variable count, with the count chosen per sample by a quality threshold.

findings.claim: TiTok tokenizes a 256x256 image into 32 discrete tokens. It reports gFID 1.97 at 256 and beats DiT-XL/2 at 512 (2.74 vs 3.04) with 64x fewer tokens and 410x faster generation.
findings.source: arXiv 2406.07550 (NeurIPS 2024; search extract); README github.com/bytedance/1d-tokenizer (verified: the project exists)
findings.relevance: Token count per item as a design variable for the future video side.

findings.claim: NVIDIA's Low Frame-rate Speech Codec uses FSQ (8 codebooks, 4 dimensions per code) at 21.5 frames/s and 1.89 kbps, and makes LLM-TTS inference about 3x faster with better intelligibility.
findings.relevance: FSQ at a low rate works at scale.

findings.claim: World models over discrete (sparse, binary) representations model more of the state space with less capacity, and in continual RL adapt faster. The authors attribute the gain to sparsity and binariness rather than discreteness itself.
findings.relevance: Weak support that discrete codes help goal B (continual learning) even when the representation keeps learning.

findings.claim: The rotation trick moves each encoder output to its codebook vector by a rotation and rescaling that is treated as constant in backprop, instead of the plain STE. It is the default in lucidrains' vector-quantize-pytorch VectorQuantize.
findings.relevance: A codec-internal gradient improvement. It does not by itself make NTP-into-tokenizer safe (GEAR's collapse is caused by the objective, not the estimator).

findings.claim: Open-MAGVIT2 factorises a 2^18 LFQ vocabulary into two sub-vocabularies (k1 = 6, k2 = 12 bits) and predicts them by 'next sub-token prediction'.
findings.relevance: Supports per-dimension or factorised heads over FSQ coordinates, which also make id drift smoother (a design inference, not a published drift result).

findings.claim: LAST trains a speech tokenizer with gradients from a frozen pretrained text LM through a light adapter, on top of a frozen speech SSL encoder, so that tokens suit sequence modelling.
findings.relevance: LM gradient shaping a tokenizer without collapse, though the LM there is frozen (the reverse of our situation).

findings.topic: codebook embeddings wired into the LLM
findings.claim: ETT connects the vision tokenizer's codebook embeddings to the LLM through an MLP, so that the LLM's loss tunes the tokenizer end-to-end while reconstruction is kept.
findings.relevance: LM input embedding computed from codebook vectors rather than a free lookup table. This is the input-side analogue of coordinate embeddings for FSQ.

live_codec_approaches.name: L1. Live codec, stop-gradient LM, re-encode from raw at read time (IRIS / REPA-E pattern)
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: The codec keeps training for the whole run on its own loss (reconstruction plus entropy). The LM loss is detached at the codes. Placeholder slots are filled at batch-cut time with the codec's current encoding of the raw clip, instead of once at a freeze, so stream codes are never stale.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: IRIS [V code]: tokenizer trained every epoch for 600 epochs; the world model encodes raw observations with the current tokenizer under no_grad. REPA-E [V code]: diffusion loss on z.detach(); VAE trained by its own losses plus alignment; from scratch gFID 4.34 vs 7.90 for a frozen-VAE baseline.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: The LM chases a moving target: code k's meaning drifts (DACT [S]), which costs LM likelihood and may read as forgetting. Encode cost at every batch cut (spec encode RTF about 0.0008 in the tree, so cheap). Requires raw clips to be available or regenerable at read time.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: High. DATA's synthetic generators regenerate clips and the spec encoder is cheap. Needs an encode-at-cut hook instead of the one-shot in-place fill of 6.2 step 3. No cadence change if the token count per clip is fixed.

live_codec_approaches.name: L2. Slow tokenizing encoder (EMA / momentum copy)
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: An EMA copy of the online encoder produces the codes the LM sees; the online encoder learns from reconstruction. The EMA momentum bounds per-step code drift and must stay below 1.0, or it becomes a freeze.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: MoCo [S]: m = 0.999 much better than 0.9 for consistency of queued keys. data2vec [S]: 0.999 -> 0.9999. V-JEPA [V config]: 0.998 -> 1.0 (reaches a freeze at the end). AQM [V code]: EMA decoder, decay 0.99.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: The codes lag the decoder: an EMA encoder paired with the online decoder is mismatched unless the decoder also has an EMA copy (as AQM keeps). A momentum that is too high amounts to a soft freeze.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: High. Adds one checkpointed tensor set with a geometry rule and a momentum lever. A code-flip-rate gauge per 1k windows makes the drift visible.

live_codec_approaches.name: L3. Bounded predictability pressure into the codec
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: Let the LM or WORLD shape the codec only through a small, clipped side term, never through NTP-via-STE: a DreamerV3-style rep loss (weight 0.1, free bits), a GEAR-style soft-assignment alignment, an EOSTok-style APR loss (decode the LM's predicted codes and reconstruct), or a LARP/CRT small AR prior inside the codec objective. Always keep reconstruction and an entropy term.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: DreamerV3 [V code]: rep 0.1, dyn 1.0, free_nats 1.0, unimix 0.01, rec 1.0. GEAR [V]: STE collapses (gFID about 105); the soft branch works and converges about 10x faster. EOSTok [S]: APR prevents collapse from scratch. GenFirst [S]: entropy preservation is essential. LARP [V], CRT [S]: 2-3x compute efficiency.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: Entropy collapse if the weight is too high or the entropy term is dropped: prediction wins against reconstruction. Adds a gradient path between packages. GEAR, EOSTok and REPA-E align to a frozen pretrained DINOv2; the from-scratch analogues are DreamerV3, APR, and self-distillation (DSD [S]).
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: Medium. The tree already has AUD_ENT_W and the aud.collapse gauge, the published counterweights. Cross-package gradient needs a COUPLING or wire and a ruling under O10. Should come after L1/L2 as an arm.

live_codec_approaches.name: L4. Fixed parameter-free lattice, live encoder and decoder, decoder rehearsal
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: FSQ's implicit codebook has no parameters, so id k always maps to the same lattice point. The encoder and decoder keep learning, and the decoder is rehearsed on stored (code, target-spectrum) pairs so old ids still decode as before.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: FSQ README [V]: no codebook parameters, no auxiliary losses. AQM [V code]: froze only the codebook once 90% of samples compressed well; encoder and decoder stayed live with self-rehearsal and an EMA decoder.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: The lattice is a fixed design choice (levels 8,5,5,5): the owner may count it as fixed. The encoder can still move audio across ids (L1/L2 handle that). The tree measured plain FSQ collapsing in 3/5 runs; iFSQ's activation [S] and the entropy bonus address that.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: High. Already the tree's quantizer; the only change is 'never stop training', plus rehearsal of old codes in the codec loss.

live_codec_approaches.name: L5. Coordinate-based LM embeddings and heads over the FSQ lattice
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: The LM input embedding for a media id is a learned function (linear or MLP) of its FSQ coordinates, not a free table row. Outputs are factorised per FSQ dimension (4 heads of 8/5/5/5 classes), predicted jointly or sequentially. Nearby lattice points share parameters, so encoder drift that moves audio to a neighbouring id costs less.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: GIVT [V]: linear input projection of real-valued vectors. ETT [S]: codebook embeddings to the LLM via MLP. Open-MAGVIT2 [S]: factorised sub-vocabulary prediction. dMel [V demo]: per-channel parallel prediction. No paper measures drift tolerance directly; this is a design inference.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: Factorised heads lose within-frame dependencies unless predicted sequentially. Changes the per-modality LM table layout and the modality-masked softmax.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: Medium. Touches the LM tables and the transport-id layout; a natural S8-style arm.

live_codec_approaches.name: L6. Remove the discrete bottleneck (continuous media tokens)
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: The LM predicts the codec's continuous latent through a GMM, diffusion or consistency head (GIVT, MAR, Transfusion, CALM, VibeVoice, MELLE), so there is no id table to drift. A live VAE is then handled as in REPA-E or GenFirst.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: GIVT [V] FID 3.35; MAR [V] FID 1.55-2.31; Transfusion [S] scales better than discrete image tokens (with a frozen VAE); CALM [S]: VAE avoids codebook collapse, consistency head 12.3x faster than RQ; VibeVoice [V] 7.5 Hz continuous.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: The tree measured no working stochastic sampler for WORLD's continuous route (GMM legality 0.54-0.64 vs 0.99) and no exact media likelihood. Transfusion and MAR still used frozen VAEs. Live-VAE collapse needs the GenFirst or REPA-E conditions.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: Low to medium now. The tree's own Route 2 evidence argues against it as the only path. It could return as a head, but it does not by itself remove freezing.

live_codec_approaches.name: L7. Training-free spectral tokens plus learned merging (the byte analogy)
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: Tokenise audio with a fixed discretisation of log-spectral channels (dMel), with no weights to freeze, and let learned components (acoustic BPE, H-Net chunking, LST patches) build larger units online, the way TOK builds on bytes.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: dMel [V code/demo]: 80 channels x 4 bits at 80 fps, training-free, beats model tokenizers on reconstruction especially out of domain (their report). Acoustic BPE [S]: 1.6-2.4x shorter sequences. LST [V]: +6.5% speech HellaSwag.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: Very long raw sequences (80 fps x 80 channels, needing parallel per-channel prediction). Reconstruction needs a vocoder (the tree uses Griffin-Lim). The binning is fixed by hand. Cuervo and Marxer [S]: BPE on units did not help.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: Medium as an arm. It sidesteps the freeze question entirely but moves the problem to the rate (next list).

live_codec_approaches.name: L8. Scheduled re-tokenisation with bounded reassignment
live_codec_approaches.mechanism: Accept a changing codec, but re-encode stored segments and re-measure the stream at scheduled points, limit how many codes change, and initialise any new or re-mapped rows from neighbours.
live_codec_approaches.evidence: HuBERT [S]: targets re-clustered between iterations. Vocabulary curriculum [S]: vocab growth alternates with training and lowers BPC. DACT [S]: relaxed-to-strict reassignment limits disruption. FOCUS/ZeTT [S]: new-embedding initialisation.
live_codec_approaches.failure_modes: Under RUN_EPOCHS = 1 every deferred retok is dropped (the Q-RUN-8 finding), so this needs RunClock.revise_epoch_length. Code-count changes move window boundaries.
live_codec_approaches.fit_here: Needed anyway if the rate becomes adaptive. Shares its mechanism with the text-TOK fix.

rate_approaches.name: R1. A lower fixed rate chosen by evidence
rate_approaches.mechanism: Pick one frame rate per modality, ideally informed by an LM-side sweep rather than a codec-only one.
rate_approaches.evidence: Mimi 12.5 Hz, chosen to approach text's ~3-4 Hz and cut AR steps [V]. VibeVoice 7.5 Hz continuous [V]. TaDiCodec 6.25 Hz [V]. LFSC 21.5 Hz FSQ, about 3x faster TTS inference [S]. SyllableLM 5-8.33 Hz, 30x less training compute [V rates / S compute]. Syllabic 4-5 Hz: >2x training time, 5x FLOPs [S]. A case study chose 12.5 Hz; 6.25 Hz lost information [S].
rate_approaches.failure_modes: Still a hand-fixed Hz, which the owner is reconsidering. The low-rate cliff may be an artefact of too-short training clips (arXiv 2606.16969 [S]); on 1 s clips this confounds any sweep.
rate_approaches.fit_here: The baseline to beat. The tree's 25 Hz LM advantage came from a 109-code SEANet codec, so a spec-codec sweep at matched context (and longer clips) is the missing measurement.

rate_approaches.name: R2. Similarity merging of adjacent codec frames
rate_approaches.mechanism: Encode at a fine base rate (e.g. the spec codec's 50 fps latent) and merge runs of similar adjacent latents: a cosine threshold (FlexiCodec), a DP segmentation (CodecSlime ScheDFR) or density-peak clustering (VARSTok). Each token carries its duration, implicitly in the id (VARSTok) or as a length field (FlexiCodec token_lengths).
rate_approaches.evidence: FlexiCodec [V]: threshold 1.0 = 12.5 Hz, 0.91 = ~8.3 Hz, 0.86 = ~6.25 Hz. FlexiSLM [V]: one LM steerable from 12.5 to 4.0 Hz. CodecSlime [S]: -32% relative WER at 40 Hz DFR. VARSTok [S]: up to 23% fewer tokens than 40 Hz.
rate_approaches.failure_modes: The average rate is still set by a threshold. Variable token counts break fixed placeholder slots F = clip_s x fps and need RunClock.revise_epoch_length. Duration-in-id multiplies the vocabulary. The decoder must be trained on merged schedules (Melt-and-Cool).
rate_approaches.fit_here: High. Cheap on CPU, sits on top of any codec, and the steady tones and silences of aud/tones are exactly what merging removes. Inference: attribute content is 36 combos (about 5.2 bits per 1 s clip), so rate need here is set by reconstruction detail at onsets and glides.

rate_approaches.name: R3. Entropy- or surprise-driven allocation
rate_approaches.mechanism: Place boundaries where a predictor is uncertain: next-byte entropy (BLT), per-segment entropy choosing among rates (TFC), or skip frames a latent predictor can fill (Elastic Time). Here the predictor could be the LM itself or WORLD's media head.
rate_approaches.evidence: BLT [V README]: entropy patches, scaling to 8B / 8T bytes; up to 50% fewer inference FLOPs [S]. TFC [S]: 75 / 37.5 / 18.75 Hz by entropy. Elastic Time [V]: lightweight causal predictor chooses skippable frames.
rate_approaches.failure_modes: The entropy threshold is a knob. Circular dependence when the predictor that sets the rate also trains on the resulting tokens (BLT used a separately trained small byte LM). Elastic Time was built on a frozen autoencoder.
rate_approaches.fit_here: Medium. Attractive because WORLD already predicts media latents, but it couples packages and needs a ruling.

rate_approaches.name: R4. Learned end-to-end chunking inside the LM
rate_approaches.mechanism: H-Net-style routing on similarity of adjacent hidden states, with a smoothing module and a ratio loss toward a target compression ratio. The LM consumes fine tokens and learns its own units.
rate_approaches.evidence: H-Net [V code]: boundary where (1 - cos(q_t, k_{t-1}))/2 > 0.5. [S]: a 1-stage byte H-Net beats a BPE Transformer when compute- and data-matched. Joint tokenization-and-LM study (arXiv 2608.17325 [S]): H-Nets learn long tokens with low overlap with subword vocabularies.
rate_approaches.failure_modes: The target ratio N is a hyperparameter. Heavy architectural change to the GRU LM. Training is less stable than fixed tokens.
rate_approaches.fit_here: Low for now (large LM surgery). Worth keeping as the principled end state for both text and audio.

rate_approaches.name: R5. LM-side merging of fixed-rate codes (acoustic BPE / latent patches)
rate_approaches.mechanism: Keep the codec at a fine fixed grid and merge frequent code n-grams into new ids (acoustic BPE, exactly TOK's mechanism), or patch them into latent units (LST).
rate_approaches.evidence: Acoustic BPE [S]: 1.6-2.4x shorter sequences, 2.8-5.0x faster inference, better syntax. LST [V]: +6.5% speech HellaSwag, gains grow with scale. Cuervo and Marxer [S]: BPE on units did not improve.
rate_approaches.failure_modes: Inherits TOK's problem: re-segmentation deferred to the epoch roll is dropped at RUN_EPOCHS = 1. Merges over a live codec's drifting ids are unstable. Mixed evidence on benefit.
rate_approaches.fit_here: Medium. Reuses TOK machinery but only helps once Q-RUN-8 option (a) exists.

rate_approaches.name: R6. Ordered, truncatable tokens (nested dropout / tail drop)
rate_approaches.mechanism: Train the codec with a random-length tail of tokens dropped, so tokens are ordered coarse to fine. At encode time, each clip gets the smallest count that meets a quality threshold, and the LM emits an end marker.
rate_approaches.evidence: FlexTok [V nested truncation; S: FID < 2 across 8-128 tokens]. ElasticTok [V: FSQ (8,8,8,5,5,5), 256-4096 tokens; S: 2-5x fewer tokens]. One-D-Piece [V: quality-controllable nested truncation].
rate_approaches.failure_modes: A quality threshold is still a knob. Coarse-to-fine 1D tokens lose the time-aligned structure that WORLD's per-frame prediction uses. A variable count per clip needs revise_epoch_length.
rate_approaches.fit_here: Medium. It matches FSQ and makes the per-clip count content-driven, but breaks WORLD's frame-aligned latents unless kept as a separate arm.

rate_approaches.name: R7. Alignment-driven rate (text- or character-aligned)
rate_approaches.mechanism: Units follow transcript characters or syllables (DyCAST, TaDiCodec text guidance, TASTE-style).
rate_approaches.evidence: DyCAST [V]: 6.2-17.5 Hz. TaDiCodec [V]: 6.25 Hz with text guidance.
rate_approaches.failure_modes: Needs transcripts or aligned text, which aud/tones lacks (captions describe attributes, not a time-aligned sequence).
rate_approaches.fit_here: Low for the current synthetic data; relevant later for real speech.

lit.reexamination_of_03_rejections:
Short answer: the cited literature supports rejecting NAIVE joint backprop (the LM's next-token or likelihood loss flowing into the codec through STE or directly). It does not support freezing the codec.
