designs.cost:
MEASURED, CPU, one thread, per LM step of 12 media clips + 4 text windows, P1:
- frozen25: 0.1355 / 0.1374 s.
- ttc25: 0.183 / 0.190 s (+35-38%). Parts: codec 0.0347 s per step (one codec step every 2 windows, 0.069 s per codec step), WORLD with the student re-encode 0.020 s, encode 0.0165 s.
- ttc25c: 0.194 / 0.197 s (+43%). The coordinate rows cost +0.01 s.
- ttcMR: 0.28 s (+106%). Parts: encode plus allocation (3 decodes) 0.0436 s, LM 0.182 s because V grows to 3264.
- ttcMRc: 0.333 s (+146%).

PROJECTION TO THE OWNER'S SHAPE. Arithmetic, NOT measured on a GPU.
- A 20k-window run at AUD_TRAIN_EVERY=4 takes about 5,000 codec steps, against 750 under AUD_FREEZE_AT=3000: the codec becomes a permanent cost.
- The EMA update is one lerp over 0.92-1.2M parameters per codec step: negligible.
- Just-in-time encoding per media window (128 positions = 5.1-5.8 s of audio) is about 7-8 ms CPU for spec encode (1.4 ms per 1 s clip).
- Allocation is about 3.6 ms per clip on CPU. In the tree it runs only at the re-segmentation act (every 3,000 windows) over the tail, not at every cut. A per-cut encode with a stored stride map costs one encode.
- The LM head grows by the extra stride blocks. With LM_VOCAB_SLOTS 4096 + 3002 media rows vs + 1002 rows, head FLOPs grow about 1.39x. A factorised head (stride class + coordinate head) with coordinate rows could remove the free per-id rows entirely; unmeasured.
- On a GPU under MPS with 12 runs per card, the 1-D conv codec is small and likely launch-bound. Its real cost is owed to R12's GPU bench arm ('codec live' vs 'codec frozen', 12 runs per card, windows/s and peak memory).
- Memory: student + teacher is about 2 x 1.2M parameters plus AdamW moments, under 30 MB per run.
designs.risks:
1) Measured losses I will not hide:
   - With the same LM rows, a live codec costs +4.1% to +8.1% LM bits/s against a frozen one.
   - The earlier area's LM bits rise +4.7% / +7.4% in the next phase (backward transfer).
   - frozen25c beat ttc25c on most understanding readings.
   - The adaptive rate LOST +10% / +13% bits/s without coordinate rows. With them it only ties (s0 only), and melody generation fell from 7/42 to 1/42.
   - At the owner's scale the codec takes about 8x more steps than here, so drift may accumulate. It must be re-measured.
2) The EMA teacher did not lower final LM bits against online codes (s0). Its measured value is smoother targets and better reconstruction. 0.999, a lower LR floor, and a code-stability anchor are untested at LM level.
3) Toy scale: 1,200 media steps, 1 s clips, 36- and 16-combo generators. Task exact metrics are near the floor: tones generation 1-8%, tones understanding 4-42%. Several arms have one seed (live25, ttcN25, ttcMRc). The 1 s clips carry the short-clip low-rate confound [S].
4) The adaptive rate needs Q-RUN-8 option (a), a frozen-surface move (137 -> 138). It inherits the unmeasured side-effect risk of a real mid-epoch act (archive: 2.189 b/B lost to 23 mostly no-op retoks), the OPT under-anneal, and MEM stale contexts. It also changes every default run past window 3000.
5) Relative-tolerance allocation spends MORE positions as the codec improves (+15-17% over 2,000 windows, s0). windows_in_epoch keeps being revised, and bits/s is a moving unit, so R-matrix rows must carry the codec step.
6) CPU cost is +35-45% per step (fixed stride) and more than double for the multi-rate arm in this prototype. The GPU cost is unmeasured.
7) Stride-1 segments bought no mel at this budget (forced 50 Hz 0.441 / 0.432 vs 25 Hz 0.430 / 0.431), so the allocator may be spending positions it does not need. An LM-aware rate-distortion allocation (the LM's measured per-stride bits) is the untested fix.
8) Griffin-Lim stays as the fixed, NON-learned default vocoder for the CPU budget. It is not absolutely necessary; a learned vocoder head is a GPU arm.
9) The lattice-locality finding (99% one-step flips) is specific to FSQ. An RVQ or VQ codec would not have it.
10) Compute used was about 85 CPU-minutes, about 5 over the ~80-minute guidance. The host was shared, so wall-clock timings carry contention noise.
11) The continuous student-latent input to the LM was NOT measured. The input 'decided by measurement' is discrete teacher ids through coordinate rows vs table rows.

scores.name: D3 — TTC: live student + EMA teacher, codes cut just in time, lattice-coordinate LM rows, nested multi-rate codec
scores.rationale: Weights: goal_a .25, goal_b .20, nothing_frozen .15, rate/tree_fit/evidence/cost .10 each (performance first). GOAL A: owns the only large measured lever in the study, lattice-coordinate media rows. D3 measured -12.9/-13.2% tones and -14.2/-15.3% melody bits/s (2 seeds). The judge replicated it in D1's independent stream harness at 2 seeds x frozen and live: -14.1% to -16.7% on the current area and -11.2% to -12.7% on B at the end, and B understanding rose 0.143/0.155 -> 0.274/0.25. ttc25c beats the proposal baseline on bits/s (-6.2% to -10.0%) and mel (-10% to -13%) at both seeds. Its high-plasticity live codec costs +4.1% to +8.1% LM bits/s against a frozen codec with the same rows. The judge's low-plasticity rerun in its harness cut that to +1.0/+1.9% (s0). GOAL B: text never moved; with 50/50 rehearsal the codec showed no forgetting; the backward-transfer cost is measured honestly (+4.7/+7.4% bits/position on the old area). Live codecs lost timbre recoverability, and it did not flag this (0.648 -> 0.481 tones s0). NOTHING FROZEN: EMA never reaches 1. The nested codec takes the Hz out of the codec. Every remaining fixed item (grid, lattice, stride set, widths) is justified. RATE: the nested codec plus a measured allocation table is the best rate answer; it reports that 'alloc' lost with table rows and tied with coord rows (1 seed). TREE FIT: the act and resume are designed but not prototyped. Its 'window' is an LM step of 16 i.i.d. examples, not a tree window, so JIT and 'no geometry change' were never exercised in stream form. EVIDENCE: the judge reproduced ttc25c s0 and flipdist s0 bit-exactly. Rate arms are single-seed, and the melody-generation win is quoted at T=1.0 while frozen25c wins at T=0.7. COST: +35-43% per step at its codec cadence; the multi-rate arm is +106-146%.

scores.name: D1 — living discrete codec behind an act-refreshed snapshot + anchor hinge, online acoustic BPE, one mid-epoch act (Q-RUN-8 option a)
scores.rationale: GOAL A: its low-plasticity live codec (floor 5e-5, anchor w10) beat the frozen codec on bits/s in 6/6 paired readings (-2.10 to -5.23) with slightly better mel. The judge reran live25 s0 bit-exactly and extended it: with lattice rows, live still beats frozen in 6/6 readings (-1.0% to -4.3%). But the gains are small. Reconstruction probe-exact fell (A -0.118/-0.055). BPE bought nothing per bit (+1.2 to +9.9 bits/s in 5/6 readings vs fixed 50 fps). The design as defaulted (live50bpe) costs +22.5% windows and +52% wall against the baseline. GOAL B: the anchor is measured load-bearing. Without it, codec BWT is +0.024/+0.025 mel and A bits/s is +4.85/+9.96 worse. The live codec neither causes nor prevents LM forgetting of A. It is the only design showing that deferral strands every mint (0 of 800,000). NOTHING FROZEN: the codec is live but barely moves (B mel 0.622 -> 0.614). Its snapshot is held for 2000 windows between acts. The learned BPE rate follows the text-TOK analogy. RATE: data-driven and content-dependent (34-43 positions/s), but measured worse per bit and dearer. TREE FIT: best by far. It prototyped RunClock.revise_epoch_length, the post-flush act, the splice after the record under the cursor, a record/byte-cursor resume with a re-measure geometry check, and cadences keyed on a run-global counter. The judge reproduced its bit-identical resume. EVIDENCE: 2 paired seeds, proper controls (frozen, free, deferred), a disclosed optimizer-aliasing bug, and every checked number reproduced exactly. COST: live codec +20% wall; the full design +52%.

scores.name: D2 — live continuous codec, chunk latents into the LM end to end, H-Net router rate
scores.rationale: GOAL A: the continuous LM interface loses on almost every LM-side reading at 2 seeds: tones understanding 0.078/0.078 vs 0.25/0.234, caption bits/byte, teacher-forced mel, generation timbre. The designer says so and recommends 'codes' as the default. The live continuous codec reconstructs well (melody ceiling 1.0). GOAL B: text and codec show no forgetting under rehearsal. The stale-latent measurement (+0.063/+0.076 mel) is the clearest case for 'persist nothing codec-dependent'. NOTHING FROZEN: fully live, with end-to-end input gradient and a learned router; only the grid is fixed. RATE: the router did not beat a fixed stride at a matched average (1 fixed seed), it adds 0.37-1.08 bits/position of duration, and it never predicts END under greedy decoding. Its window-denominated media geometry is a genuinely useful idea: a variable rate with no Q-RUN-8 for media. TREE FIT: wires 22/25 and several signature moves; the geometry idea is good. EVIDENCE: base and d2 have 2 seeds, ablations 1. Confounds: the LM parameter count differs (289k vs 523k), and the text-only P1 differs by 0.2 bits/byte under identical training. It found and fixed a real loss-balancing defect; the judge reproduced dbg_grad exactly and the weight-1.0 crowding (9.62 vs 1.80). COST: the live codec is +65% per media step over the same design frozen.

judge.winner: D3 (two-timescale live codec: EMA teacher, codes cut just in time, lattice-coordinate LM rows, nested multi-rate codec), with D1's stream mechanics (the Q-RUN-8 option (a) act, RunClock.revise_epoch_length, cursor resume, anchor hinge, BPE arm) grafted on as the prerequisite stage S0b and the drift stack, and D2's window geometry, continuous route and loss-balance gauges kept as arms.
grafts: From D1: RunClock.revise_epoch_length(n) and the retok act moved from _flush into run after the flush, with the batch empty. The splice goes after the record under the cursor, the prefix is asserted preserved and the cursor kept, and resume uses a record/byte cursor that re-measures windows_in_epoch and refuses on mismatch. The prototype was bit-identical across 3 post-save acts, and the judge reproduced it. It becomes stage S0b, the prerequisite that also makes text retok live.
From D1: every cadence is keyed on a checkpointed run-global counter, never a loop-local one. D1's first resume test failed with max |dloss| 0.0503 for exactly this reason.

From D1: the assignment-stability anchor hinge AUD_ANCHOR_W 10 x mean relu(|b - q_target| - 0.25)^2, retargeted from the act snapshot to the EMA teacher's lattice point. Codec-only it cut flips 3x (0.255 -> 0.082 per 50 steps) and improved area-A mel (0.506 -> 0.475). The LM-level control arm without it forgot more (A bits/s +4.85/+9.96).

From D1: a readiness Gate replaces the freeze Gate; the OPT 'codec' group keeps a floor of 0.05 x peak; the codec LR re-warms when a new media area arrives (codec-only, one seed: B mel 0.569 vs 0.577 and A mel 0.489 vs 0.499).
From D1: online acoustic BPE over lattice ids becomes AUD_RATE_MODE='bpe', with the aud.bpe.stranded counter that must read 0 under S0b (the deferred control stranded 0 of 800,000 positions).
From D1: duration-governed END for known-length families under variable-rate arms. Predicted END left 33-62 of 64-108 BPE clips short; duration-governed END left 0 short.
From D1: codec-invariant primary readings, bits/s tagged with the codec version, and a per-area codec-BWT row.

From D2: the window-denominated media geometry (media windows per phase fixed at compose from DATA_TEXT_SHARE, packed just in time) as the arm DATA_MEDIA_GEOMETRY='windows'. It lets any variable-rate arm run with no media re-splice.

From D2: the continuous chunk-insert route (GMM, duration and END heads, H-Net router) as the S8 arm AUD_LM_IO='continuous', with LM_MEDIA_GMM_W 0.1 and the lm.media.gmm_grad_ratio gauge. Its defect was reproduced: at weight 1.0 the GMM gradient norm is 9.62 against caption CE 1.80.
From D2: persist nothing codec-dependent (stale latents cost +0.063/+0.076 mel), and CKPT refuses a mixed-origin restore of aud versus lm.media_*.
From D2: the arm AUD_LM_GRAD='input' (continuous only) and the latent std / participation-ratio collapse gauges.

Judge addition: DATA_MEDIA_REHEARSE 0.25 (earlier media areas rehearsed in the LM stream). In the judge's 2-seed replication, coordinate rows raised old-area interference: A bits/s rose +53.3 to +58.9 after B, against +37.3 to +38.7 with table rows.

Judge addition: a per-attribute codec-ceiling guard. Every live D3 arm lost timbre recoverability on reconstructions (tones 0.648/0.602 -> 0.481/0.556; melody 0.641/0.656 -> 0.500/0.609) while every other attribute rose.

what_stays_fixed.thing: Within one training window, every media code id and the LM rows that read it come from ONE codec state (the EMA teacher at cut time)
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: If one window mixed codec states, one id would denote two sounds inside a single gradient step, and nothing could learn it. The teacher itself moves every codec step, so this is consistency, not a freeze.

what_stays_fixed.thing: The audio analysis grid within a run: DATA_AUD_SR 8000, STFT n_fft 512, hop 160 (50 frames/s)
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: It is the audio unit, the analogue of the byte. Every codec tensor (257 input bins, the frame axis) and every stride block is shaped by it, and checkpoints load by shape. Its VALUE is a lever chosen per run, EXACT across a resume. A learned front end (the 'wave' arm) is the live alternative; it did not reach phase at CPU budget (§6.1, measured).

what_stays_fixed.thing: The FSQ lattice (AUD_LEVELS 8,5,5,5 -> 1000 points per stride block; id k is lattice point k)
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: It has no parameters, so it freezes nothing learned. It is the media address space. LM coordinate rows, tally keys and merge expansions are indexed by it, so changing it mid-run redefines every id. A change goes through the versioned-block handover arm (new block, nearest-row init), never silently.

what_stays_fixed.thing: The stride set {1,2,4} and the 80 ms segment (AUD_STRIDES, AUD_SEG_FRAMES) of the nested codec
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: They set the number of media id blocks and the schedules the decoder is trained on; both are tensor extents. The set can widen by appending a block (e.g. stride 8). The rate used WITHIN the set is a lever, not fixed.

what_stays_fixed.thing: Tensor widths and preallocated extents: codec D/H, LM_WIDTH/LM_CTX, WORLD_LAT, media row slots
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: Checkpoints load by tensor shape, and the tree has no growth operator (Net2Net-style widening). Slots are MAY_WIDEN across a resume, as LM_VOCAB_SLOTS already is.

what_stays_fixed.thing: Append-only expansions of minted ids (text id2bytes; media merges under the 'bpe' arm)
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: A minted id must keep what it expands to. Otherwise its row's meaning changes silently, and a resume cannot rebuild the tail from the saved vocabulary or merges.

what_stays_fixed.thing: The re-segmentation act runs only at a flush boundary with an empty batch, splices after the unit under the cursor, and keeps the consumed prefix
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: Otherwise one batch holds bounds from two segmentations, or a partly consumed unit is re-cut, and windows are replayed or skipped. The prototype asserts this at every act.

what_stays_fixed.thing: No next-token (likelihood) gradient from the LM into the codec through STE or through the codec's own targets
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: This is not a freeze; the codec trains all run on its own loss. It bans the one coupling with measured collapse: GEAR gFID about 105 [V]; in D2, undetached targets cut latent PR to 2.45 and understanding to 0.016 (1 seed). Bounded couplings (DreamerV3 rep term, input-side gradient) remain lever-gated arms.

what_stays_fixed.thing: Measurement contracts: fixed held-out and probe clips and seeds, EVAL frozen_rng, analytic inverses, evals that store clips rather than codes
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: Drift, forgetting, flip rates and R-matrix rows are only defined against inputs that do not move. They are not learned representations.

what_stays_fixed.thing: Software contracts named 'frozen': Configs, §7 entry-point signatures, record dataclasses, once-resolved wires
what_stays_fixed.why_absolutely_necessary: These are Ownership Spine contracts, outside the owner's objection, and they are what makes every lever and every reading auditable.

open_questions.question: Do fixed NON-learned transforms count as 'absolutely necessary': the STFT analysis grid, the FSQ lattice, and Griffin-Lim?
open_questions.recommendation: The grid and the lattice: yes, as the audio analogue of bytes, with their learned alternatives built as arms ('wave' front end; versioned-block handover for a lattice change). Griffin-Lim: no. Build a learned iSTFT/vocoder head as an S8/GPU arm judged on DATA.recover of decoded audio, and keep Griffin-Lim as the CPU default until that arm wins.
open_questions.why: The owner objects to learned things that stop learning and to rates fixed by hand. The grid and the lattice carry no parameters and are what give an id its address. Griffin-Lim is a fixed stage where a learned one exists. The fall in timbre recovery under live codecs (0.648 -> 0.481) may come from this stage.

open_questions.question: The frame rate: ship 25 Hz as a measured default on the nested codec, or ship an adaptive rate now?
open_questions.recommendation: Ship AUD_RATE_MODE='fixed', AUD_RATE_STRIDE=2 on the nested codec. Build 'alloc', 'bpe' and 'router' as arms and re-decide at S5 on GPU with 2-4 s clips by the pre-declared rule. Include 12.5 Hz in the sweep.
open_questions.why: Every adaptive route lost or tied on the LM side at toy scale (D3 +10/+13% with table rows, a tie with coordinate rows; D1 BPE +0.5-5%; D2's router worse). The nested codec already removes the Hz from the codec, so changing the rate is a lever flip.

open_questions.question: Codec plasticity default: how fast should a never-frozen codec move?
open_questions.recommendation: Floor 0.05 x peak (5e-5), plus a re-warm to 0.3 x peak ramped over 100 codec steps whenever a new media area arrives, decaying back over 1200 windows. Add the anchor hinge (w 10, margin 0.25) toward the teacher's lattice point, the EMA teacher at 0.995, and 50% codec rehearsal. S3 runs the codec-only matrix and S5 the LM-level matrix, 2 seeds each, and the default follows the pre-declared rule.
open_questions.why: Measured in both harnesses: low plasticity costs the LM nothing (D1 6/6 readings better than frozen; D3-cold +1.0/+1.9%) but adapts little to a new area (melody mel -3.9%). High plasticity adapts (-12%) for +4-8% LM bits. An abrupt 6x jump with no anchor hurt the old area (+6.4%). Re-warm on novelty spends plasticity where the owner's goals need it. The combination is unmeasured at LM level and is labelled so.

open_questions.question: Adopt Q-RUN-8 option (a) (stage S0b), knowing it changes every default run past window 3000 because TOK_RETOK_EVERY ships at 3000?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes; build it first, as S0b. Take the owed paired measurement (TOK_RETOK_EVERY 0 / 3000 / 1000 at RUN_EPOCHS=1, 2 seeds, held-out bits/byte) before shipping the default. Keep 3000 unless both seeds show held-out bits/byte worse than seed noise; then set the default by the measurement and report it.
open_questions.why: The text segmentation is the largest learned thing the tree holds frozen today: about 600 mints per run are stranded, and the lever decides nothing at any epoch count. The same act serves the adaptive-rate media arms. The prototype showed the mechanics (12 acts, bit-identical resume). The archive's 2.189 bits/byte side-effect loss is the risk to watch; a real mid-epoch text retok has never been measured.

open_questions.question: The OPT horizon after a mid-epoch act: revise it, or report the residual?
open_questions.recommendation: Build OPT.revise_horizon, default on (OPT_HORIZON_REVISE True), called by the act. Keep opt.horizon.residual_steps as the reading.
open_questions.why: Each act changes the remaining windows: -6.9% over a run in D1's BPE prototype. Q-OPT-5's under-anneal would then occur inside every run, and a schedule fixed at build is itself a hand-fixed quantity the instruction targets.

open_questions.question: Lattice-coordinate media rows by default, given that they raise interference between media areas?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes, LM_MEDIA_ROWS='coord' by default, paired with DATA_MEDIA_REHEARSE 0.25. Keep 'table' as the arm.
open_questions.why: This is the only large, replicated gain: -11% to -17% on the current area in two harnesses at 2 seeds, with understanding up. Without media rehearsal the old area rose +53 to +59 bits/s against +37 to +39 with table rows. Rehearsal of earlier media areas measurably held them (D2, D3).

open_questions.question: Media geometry: inline placeholders (R1) or window-denominated media windows (D2)?
open_questions.recommendation: Inline by default (DATA_MEDIA_GEOMETRY='inline'), filled just in time. Build 'windows' as an arm.
open_questions.why: Inline keeps R4's final-coordinate stream and supports real interleaved audio+text documents later. At the fixed-stride default it needs no act. 'windows' lets any variable-rate arm run with no media re-splice and is cheap to keep.

open_questions.question: The continuous media route (D2): promote it, or keep it as an arm?
open_questions.recommendation: Keep it as the S8 arm AUD_LM_IO='continuous', off by default, with LM_MEDIA_GMM_W 0.1 and the gradient-ratio gauge. The earlier §16 Q3 (the continuous insert for understanding) stays an arm as written.
open_questions.why: It lost on nearly every LM-side reading (2 seeds), carries confounds (LM size, initialisation) that a parameter-matched rerun should remove, and its head silently crowds out text at weight 1.0.

open_questions.question: Should the LM or WORLD shape the codec at all?
open_questions.recommendation: Default is none: stop-gradient at integer ids, and WORLD's target is stop-gradient. Build AUD_LM_GRAD='rep' (DreamerV3-style bounded term, weight 0.1, 1 nat free bits) and 'input' (continuous route) as arms under the collapse gauges.
open_questions.why: The literature and D2 show that likelihood-into-codec collapses or concentrates the latent. Bounded terms are published remedies but unmeasured here.

open_questions.question: Every live codec improved mel but lost timbre recovery on reconstructions. Is that acceptable?
open_questions.recommendation: No. Add a per-attribute codec-ceiling guard: aud.ceiling_drop fires when any attribute's recover rate falls below its readiness value by more than 0.05. Open an S3 investigation arm: a harmonic or multi-resolution spectral loss term, and the learned vocoder arm.
open_questions.why: DATA.recover is the primary reading and generation is scored through it. Timbre fell 0.648/0.602 -> 0.481/0.556 (tones) and 0.641/0.656 -> 0.500/0.609 (melody) in D3's live arms while other attributes rose. D1's recon probe-exact fell for every live arm on A.

open_questions.question: WORLD's world_proj stays born zero with no gradient (WORLD_FEEDBACK False). Is that a frozen learned parameter?
open_questions.recommendation: Leave it as it is, an off-by-default arm, until the GPU feedback test of Q-WORLD-10 runs. The media forecast stays born zero as §10 says.
open_questions.why: It is a parameter held at zero by a lever pending a measurement, not a codec issue. Turning it on untested risks the LM path that is working.

open_questions.question: The SIG signature width is fixed from build-time bytes_per_token for the life of the run. Re-derive it at acts?
open_questions.recommendation: Not now. S0b reports how far bytes_per_token moves across acts on the owner's stream. If it moves by more than 5%, a follow-up ruling adds DOM reservoir re-slicing and a width re-derive.
open_questions.why: Changing it mid-run forces DOM re-slicing and rekey. Its magnitude under a live retok is unmeasured, and the cost is real.

open_questions.question: Codec retraining on real data (old §16 Q11)
open_questions.recommendation: The live codec adapts in place, with the re-warm on the real area's arrival. The versioned-block handover remains only for an arch or lattice change.
open_questions.why: Code meaning is no longer frozen within a run: codes are cut just in time and nothing persists them, so a handover is needed only when the id address space itself changes.

judge.dissent:
The strongest case against picking D3 is that D1 should win with coordinate rows grafted onto it.

(1) The judge's own runs favour D1's low-plasticity regime on the LM side. With lattice rows, D1's live codec beat the frozen codec in 6 of 6 paired readings. D3's hot live codec lost to its frozen control by +4.1% to +8.1% with the same rows, and in D3's harness only the judge's cold arm closed that gap, to +1.0/+1.9% at one seed.

(2) D3 never ran a stream. Its 'window' is one LM step of 16 independently drawn examples, so its claims were never exercised in the tree's actual shape: just-in-time encoding with no geometry change, the act, and resume. D1 built and bit-verified exactly those mechanics.

(3) D3's distinctive pieces did not pay at toy scale:
- the EMA teacher did not lower final LM bits against online codes (s0);
- the adaptive nested rate lost with table rows and tied with coordinate rows at one seed, dropping melody generation 7/42 -> 1/42 at +72% CPU;
- nested at stride 2 beating spec25 is a single seed.

(4) D3's mel gains are partly an artefact of a shorter codec phase (1500 steps against D1's 4000). A codec that had not converged keeps improving whatever else is done.

(5) On the rate, the owner's own instinct (nothing fixed by hand) argues for D1's learned BPE rate as the default: it reuses the text tokenizer's machinery and is exactly what S0b unlocks. Shipping a fixed stride 2 can be read as keeping 25 Hz under a new name.

The judge's answer: D3's EMA, just-in-time encoding and coordinate rows are what carry the performance. D1's mechanics are grafted whole as S0b, and D1's anchor, floor and re-warm are part of the default drift stack. A fixed stride is the default only because every adaptive route, BPE included, measured worse or tied, and the owner's standing rule is that performance decides. The pre-declared S5 rule lets 'bpe' or 'alloc' take the default the moment it wins on GPU with realistic clip lengths.

A second dissent concerns coordinate rows. Their gain may be a small-data effect: 1000 free rows are starved at 600-1200 media steps. They measurably increase interference between media areas. At the owner's 20k-window scale the gain could shrink while the interference remains, so the S5 matrix must keep 'table' as a live arm, not a formality.
judge.synthesis_markdown:
## 0b. Nothing frozen: the live-codec revision — binding over everything below, §0 included

> Owner, 2026-09-25: "I don't like the idea of frozen codecs, I don't want anything frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary. I am also reconsidering the hz. Otherwise things look pretty good."

**Scope.** In this instruction, "frozen" means one of two things:
- a learned thing that stops learning;
- a representation rate or size fixed by hand.

These are not what the owner objects to, and they stay: frozen Configs, frozen §7 entry-point signatures, frozen record dataclasses, once-resolved wires, EVAL `frozen_rng`, and the fixed held-out sets. They are software and measurement contracts.

**Precedence.** Where 0b disagrees with §0 or any later section, 0b wins. Everything 0b does not touch stands as written.

**Evidence.**
- Three prototyped designs:
  - D1: a living discrete codec with a learned BPE rate and one mid-epoch act.
  - D2: a live continuous codec with a learned router.
  - D3: a two-timescale EMA teacher, lattice-coordinate rows and a nested multi-rate codec.
- The judge's re-runs, which reproduced one headline per design bit-exactly.
- Five new judge arms.
- Conditions: CPU, one thread, toy scale, synthetic aud/tones followed by aud/melody, GRU width 128, 1-2 seeds.
- Every number here is a signal, not a result.
- Location: `…/scratchpad/mm2/{d1,d2,d3,judge}`, to be archived under `results/multimodal_live_codec_2026-09-25/`.

### 0b.1 Decisions

**L1 — THE CODEC NEVER STOPS TRAINING.**
- `AUD_FREEZE_AT` defaults to 0, meaning never. A value > 0 remains only as the frozen-codec **control arm**: goal-B readings need the baseline.
- The freeze Gate becomes a **readiness Gate**, `AUD.ready`. It fires once when all three hold:
  - `codes_used ≥ AUD_COLLAPSE_MIN`;
  - `rms_ratio ≥ AUD_QUIET_MIN`;
  - the DATA.recover ceiling on reconstructions ≥ `AUD_READY_CEIL` (0.30, S3's acceptance figure).
- The Gate stops nothing.
- The startup refusal becomes: refuse a phase schedule whose first media LM phase starts before `AUD_READY_MIN`. That is 3000 U.Windows, the old freeze window, now a minimum and not a stop.
- If the Gate has not fired when a media phase starts, the phase runs anyway. `aud.ready.late` fires (PRESENT-and-0 while armed), and a warning names the failing gauge.
- The OPT `'codec'` group never retires; R13's retirement is void.

```
window 0 ........ AUD_READY_MIN (3000) ......................................................... 20000
| text phases; student+teacher codec trains on | readiness Gate | media phases: codes cut just in time by the
| DATA.media_batch every AUD_TRAIN_EVERY       | (fires once)   | teacher; codec keeps training (floor, re-warm
|                                              |                | at each new media area); OPT/FAB shift stamp
| S0b act every TOK_RETOK_EVERY windows: text tail re-tokenised (+ media tail under 'alloc' / 'bpe')      |
```

**L2 — CODES ARE CUT, NOT STORED.**
- R1's layout stays: placeholders in final coordinates, with F known at compose under the fixed-rate default.
- The placeholders are filled **just in time**. An A-stage `AUD.encode` at window cut writes the codes of every clip the window overlaps, using the tokenizing codec as it stands (L3).
- Deleted:
  - the one-shot in-place fill at the freeze (old §6.2 step 3);
  - the "AUD.encode at the epoch roll" row.
- The one absolutely necessary property holds by construction: within a window, code ids and LM rows refer to one codec state.
- **Nothing persists a media code as truth.** DOM reservoirs, EVAL prompts, generated samples and any MEM-over-media entry hold **clip references**: area, clip index and seed, or the waveform for a real area. Each re-encodes at its own rekey or probe time.
- §3.1's "everything persisted stores ABSOLUTE ids" stays for text and for a media id's transport address. It no longer promises that a media id's meaning is stable.
- Measured cost of persisting instead:
  - stale latents decoded by a later decoder: +0.063/+0.076 mel (D2, 2 seeds);
  - codes 600 LM steps stale: +10.2%/+15.1% LM bits/position (D3, 2 seeds).

**L3 — THE TOKENIZING CODEC IS AN EMA TEACHER OF A LIVE STUDENT.**
- The student trains on its own loss (L4).
- The teacher is the EMA of every student parameter, decay `AUD_EMA` 0.995 per codec step. The teacher:
  - supplies every id the LM sees;
  - decodes every generated id;
  - gives WORLD its target.
- `AUD_EMA ≥ 1` is refused unless `AUD_FREEZE_AT > 0`. `AUD_EMA = 0` is the online-codes arm.
- Measured (D3):
  - short-horizon code flips per 50 codec steps: 0.09-0.15, against 0.47-0.50 online (2 seeds);
  - the teacher reconstructs better than the student: tones log-mag L1 0.624/0.604 vs 0.651/0.639;
  - final LM bits are equal to online codes (111.53 vs 112.35 bits/s, seed 0 only).
- The EMA does **not** bound cumulative drift: 0.62 of probe frames change over 500 codec steps. L4 bounds it.

**L4 — PLASTICITY IS A MEASURED DIAL.**
The frontier (0b.2):
- at low plasticity, a live codec costs the LM nothing and gains a little reconstruction;
- at high plasticity, it gains 10-13% mel, most on the newest area, for +4-8% LM bits per audio-second;
- an abrupt learning-rate jump without the anchor hurts the old area.

Default stack:
- **Learning rate.** The `'codec'` group peaks at `OPT_CODEC_LR` 1e-3 during the readiness phase and decays to `OPT_CODEC_LR_MIN_FRAC` 0.05 (5e-5). It never reaches zero, following the `OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC` precedent.
- **Re-warm on novelty.** When a media area enters the schedule:
  - the group ramps to `AUD_REWARM` 0.3 × peak (3e-4) over 100 codec steps;
  - it decays back to the floor over `AUD_REWARM_WINDOWS` 1200, which is 300 codec steps at `AUD_TRAIN_EVERY` 4, the dose D1 measured;
  - the same event stamps the self-inflicted shift for OPT and FAB.
- **Assignment-stability anchor.** `AUD_ANCHOR_W` 10 × mean relu(|b − q_teacher| − `AUD_ANCHOR_MARGIN` 0.25)² on all crops. Here b is the student's pre-rounding FSQ value and q_teacher is the teacher's lattice point for the same crop.
- **Codec rehearsal.** `AUD_REHEARSE` 0.5 of every codec batch comes from earlier media areas, regenerated from clip references.
- **Cadence.** `AUD_TRAIN_EVERY` 4 windows for the whole run.

Each piece was measured beneficial in its own harness. **The combination (EMA + anchor + re-warm) is unmeasured at LM level.** S3 and S5 measure it with a pre-declared rule (§13).

**L5 — LM MEDIA ROWS ARE FUNCTIONS OF LATTICE COORDINATES.**
- `LM_MEDIA_ROWS='coord'` is the new default; `'table'` (§3's free rows) is kept as an arm.
- A media id's input vector = learned per-digit vectors (4 FSQ digits plus a stride-block slot) + a zero-initialised free residual row.
- Its logit = (o·C_head)·Pᵀ + a zero-initialised free logit.
- This is the largest measured lever of the study, replicated in two independent harnesses at 2 seeds each:
  - D3: −12.9/−13.2% tones and −14.2/−15.3% melody bits/s;
  - judge in D1's stream harness, current area: −14.8/−16.7% frozen, −14.1/−15.9% live;
  - B at the end: −11.2% to −12.7%;
  - B understanding exact: 0.143/0.155 → 0.274/0.25.
- Why it works:
  - FSQ drift is local: 98.9-100% of flips under the teacher move one lattice step (D3, 2 seeds);
  - 1000 free rows are data-starved at this budget.
- **Cost:** more interference between media areas. With no media rehearsal, the earlier area's bits/s rose +53.3 to +58.9 after the next area, against +37.3 to +38.7 with table rows (judge, 2 seeds). The end level still ties or beats table rows. Hence L6.

**L6 — EARLIER MEDIA AREAS ARE REHEARSED IN THE LM STREAM.**
- New lever `DATA_MEDIA_REHEARSE` 0.25: inside a media phase, that share of media windows is drawn from earlier media areas listed in the phase. The newest area gets the rest.
- `DATA_TEXT_SHARE` 0.3 is unchanged.
- Measured:
  - with no LM media rehearsal, the earlier area's understanding reads 0.0 at the end in every D1 arm, and its caption bits/byte rises 0.30-0.35 → 2.30-2.68;
  - 25% rehearsal held tones understanding (D2 base 0.25 → 0.234);
  - one-third rehearsal held tones bits flat under coordinate rows (D3 frozen25c 3.612 → 3.615 bits/position).

**L7 — THE FRAME RATE IS NOT A CODEC CONSTANT.**
- `AUD_ARCH='nested'` is the new default (§6.1). On the 50 frames/s analysis grid, each 80 ms segment is coded at stride 1, 2 or 4 (50 / 25 / 12.5 Hz). One decoder decodes any stride map, so changing the rate needs no retraining.
- The LM-side rate is the lever `AUD_RATE_MODE`:
  - `'fixed'` (default): `AUD_RATE_STRIDE` 2, i.e. 25 Hz;
  - `'alloc'`: each segment gets the coarsest stride whose teacher reconstruction error is within (1+`AUD_RATE_TOL`) of the finest;
  - `'bpe'`: online acoustic BPE over lattice ids, TOK's mint mechanism;
  - `'router'`: H-Net boundaries, continuous route only.
- `'fixed'` at stride 2 is a **measured default, not a constant**. At toy scale no adaptive route beat it on the LM side (0b.2), and forced 12.5 Hz cost +12% codec mel. It is re-decided at S5 by the rule in §16 Q2.
- Under `'fixed'`, the modality mask admits only the active stride block, so unused blocks take no softmax mass.
- `'alloc'` and `'bpe'` change a clip's position count, so they need L8.
- §8 generation: under `'fixed'`, F codes then forced END, as before. Under `'alloc'` or `'bpe'`, END is duration-governed for known-length families and predicted with a clip-length guard otherwise. Measured in D1: predicted END left 33-62 of 64-108 clips short; duration-governed END left 0 short.

**L8 — MID-EPOCH RE-SEGMENTATION IS A PREREQUISITE STAGE, S0b (Q-RUN-8 OPTION (a)).**
- The text tokenizer is the largest learned thing the tree freezes today. At `RUN_EPOCHS=1`, every retok waits for a roll that never comes:
  - about 600 mints per 20k-window run are stranded (arithmetic from `TOK_GROW_EVERY` 200 × burst 6);
  - `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` decides nothing at any `RUN_EPOCHS` (measured 2026-09-24).
- S0b builds `RunClock.revise_epoch_length(n)` and moves the act from `_flush` into `run`, after the flush while the batch is empty. The act:
  1. splices at the cursor;
  2. re-segments the tail only;
  3. revises the epoch length with the cursor kept.
- One act serves both the text retok and the variable-rate media arms.
- Prototyped in D1:
  - 12 acts; every prefix-preserved and cursor-kept assertion passed; no window replayed or skipped;
  - save/restore is bit-identical across 3 post-save acts (the judge re-ran it);
  - the deferred control stranded all 192 mints (0 of 800,000 positions), while the act put 12.0-12.1% minted ids into consumed data.
- The **text** half has never been exercised. The owed paired measurement comes first (§13 S0b).

**L9 — WORLD'S MEDIA TARGET IS THE TEACHER, STOP-GRADIENT, WITH HORIZONS IN MILLISECONDS** (§10).

**L10 — NO NEXT-TOKEN GRADIENT INTO THE CODEC; BOUNDED COUPLINGS ARE ARMS.**
- The old rejection of "joint codec+LM backprop" is narrowed to: *the LM's likelihood loss flowing into the codec through STE or through the codec's own targets*. Evidence against that coupling:
  - GEAR, gFID about 105 [V];
  - in D2 it concentrated the latent (PR 2.45 vs 3.71/4.40) and cut understanding to 0.016 (1 seed).
- A codec trained concurrently on its own loss is the default (L1).
- Arms, off by default:
  - `AUD_LM_GRAD='rep'`: a DreamerV3-style bounded predictability term, weight 0.1, 1 nat of free bits;
  - `AUD_LM_GRAD='input'`: continuous route only.

**L11 — READINGS SURVIVE A MOVING CODEC.**
- Primary R-matrix media readings are codec-invariant:
  - DATA.recover exact and per attribute (generation, understanding, codec ceiling);
  - mel;
  - a2t caption bits/byte;
  - grounding bits per clip.
- Bits per audio-second stays, because it is rate-invariant, but it is tagged with the teacher step. Its alphabet moves: a codec that spends more entropy earns more bits, so two arms' bits/s over different codecs are not a like-for-like LM comparison.
- New rows per area:
  - codec BWT: mel and per-attribute ceiling of area a at every later phase end;
  - flip rate, and cumulative flip since readiness, on a fixed probe set;
  - a stale-code probe: LM bits on current codes vs codes N windows old.
- bits/code is secondary.
- A per-attribute ceiling guard, `aud.ceiling_drop`, is armed (0b.2, row "timbre").

**L12 — GEOMETRY IS EXACT ONLY WHERE A SHAPE OR AN ID ADDRESS DEPENDS ON IT.** `aud.version` becomes a READING: teacher step plus a weight hash at save (§11).

## 6. Codecs (replaces §6)

### 6.1 AUD default: 'nested' spectral FSQ on a 50 frames/s grid

- **Features.** STFT log-magnitude, n_fft 512, hop 160 at `DATA_AUD_SR` 8000: 50 frames/s, 20 ms per frame. This grid is the audio unit.
- **Encoder.** Conv1d(257→256, k3), ELU, Conv1d(256→256, k3), ELU, Conv1d(256→64, k1). The result is a 50 frames/s, 64-d latent with no strided layer.
- **Quantiser.**
  - Each 80 ms segment (`AUD_SEG_FRAMES` 4) is coded at a stride s ∈ `AUD_STRIDES` {1,2,4}.
  - FSQ 8,5,5,5 (with the iFSQ activation and the entropy bonus) quantises the s-average-pooled latent.
  - The id is block(s) × 1000 + code.
  - The decoder receives each quantised vector repeated s times.
- **Decoder.** Conv1d(64→256, k3), ELU, two Conv1d(256→256, k3) with ELU, Conv1d(256→257, k1), predicting log-magnitude.
- **Rate dropout.** In training, every segment of every crop gets a random stride, so one decoder decodes any stride map.
- **Waveform.** Griffin-Lim 32 (fixed, not learned; the learned vocoder is an arm).
- **Loss.** L1 on log-magnitude + 2 × L1 on magnitude + entropy bonus (`AUD_ENT_W` 1.0) + the anchor hinge (L4).
- **Training crops.** `AUD_CROP_S` 0.64 s, a whole number of 80 ms segments.

Measured (D3, CPU, one thread):
- At forced stride 2, the nested codec matched or beat the dedicated 25 Hz codec on the LM side at seed 0: −2.6% tones and −4.7% melody bits/s, tones mel 0.4438 vs 0.4712.
- Codec-side trade at the end of the drift sweep (teacher 0.995; seeds 0/1). Cells are positions/s, then mel.

| 'alloc' rho 0.1 | 22.0 / 22.8, 0.433 / 0.429 | 26.5 / 26.5, 0.518 / 0.520 |
| 'alloc' rho 0.5 | 16.3 / 16.9, 0.443 / 0.439 | 16.9 / 17.4, 0.539 / 0.549 |
| fixed 25 Hz | 26, 0.430 / 0.431 | 26, 0.521 / 0.531 |

- `'wave'`: SEANet, a GPU arm, unchanged.

**Pre-declared switch.** If S3 does not reproduce "nested at stride 2 ≥ 'spec' on mel, codes used and per-attribute ceiling" at 2 seeds, `AUD_ARCH` reverts to `'spec'`, and the rate levers act through separate per-rate codecs.

### 6.2 Training: for the whole run

1. **Readiness phase.** From window 0 until the media phases, `AUD.loss_terms` runs on `DATA.media_batch` clips every `AUD_TRAIN_EVERY` (4) windows, under OPT group `'codec'` with its own warmup and decay toward the floor.
2. **After readiness.** The codec keeps training at the same cadence. Each batch is 16 crops:
   - (1 − `AUD_REHEARSE`) from the current media areas;
   - `AUD_REHEARSE` (0.5) from earlier media areas, drawn only from clips the stream has already consumed and regenerated from clip references.
3. **Teacher update.** After each codec step, the teacher takes one EMA update (`AUD_EMA` 0.995).
4. **Anchor.** The hinge targets the teacher's lattice point for the same crop, so the student moves freely inside an FSQ cell and is pushed back only before a code would flip.
5. **Re-warm.** At each media-area arrival, the group re-warms (L4) and the OPT/FAB shift is stamped.
6. **Encoding.** `AUD.encode(aud, codec, clips, *, stride_map=None)` runs at window cut with the teacher. It writes into R1's placeholders; under `'alloc'` it follows the clip's stored stride map.
7. **No LM next-token gradient reaches the codec.** Codes are integers. WORLD's target is also stop-gradient.

### 6.3 Drift: what it costs and what bounds it

- **Churn is intrinsic.** Without control, 25-42% (D1) and 47-50% (D3) of probe frames flip per 50 codec steps at learning rate 3e-4. Bounds:
  - EMA 0.995: 9-15%;
  - anchor w10 at 5e-5: 5-8%.
- **Cumulative change** after about 300 anchored codec steps: 25-28% of old-area frames (D1). At the owner's scale, about 5,000 codec steps, it will be larger. `aud.flip_cum` reports it.
- **Drift is local on the lattice.** 98.9-100% of flips under the teacher move one step (D3, 2 seeds; the judge reproduced seed 0). Coordinate rows exploit this (L5).
- **Stale ids never reach the LM or eval,** because codes are cut just in time and nothing persists them.
- **What remains** is the LM re-learning a moving target:
  - D3 measured +4.7/+7.4% bits/position on the old area across the next phase at high plasticity;
  - D1 measured none at low plasticity.
- **The frozen codec's one guarantee, old-code decodability (AQM), is replaced by a measured codec-BWT row.** Measured values:
  - anchored live arms +0.0008 to +0.0103 mel (D1);
  - unanchored +0.024/+0.025 mel (D1);
  - tones mel improved through the melody phase under 50/50 rehearsal (D3).
- **An open defect.** Timbre recovery on reconstructions fell in every live D3 arm while every other attribute rose (0b.2, row 13). The guard `aud.ceiling_drop` fires when any attribute's recover rate falls more than 0.05 below its readiness value. S3 opens a harmonic / multi-resolution spectral loss arm to address it.

## 10. WORLD deltas

- **Target.**
  - `WORLD.media_terms` predicts the **teacher's** 64-d pre-quantisation latent, under stop-gradient.
  - Under 'nested', the latent is pooled to 25 Hz.
  - The input is the teacher's latent too (`WORLD_MEDIA_INPUT` 'teacher'), so the LM and WORLD read one codec state per window.
  - D3's student-input form is the arm.
- **Horizons** are declared in milliseconds (`WORLD_MEDIA_HORIZONS_MS` '40,200') and converted through derive at the latent rate. They never move with the LM-side rate.

- **No VICReg on this path.** The reason changes: WORLD's gradient never reaches the codec, and the codec's reconstruction, entropy bonus and anchor keep the target informative.
  - Gauges `aud.target_std` and `aud.target_pr` are armed; `aud.collapse` fires on either falling below its floor.
  - VICReg stays on WORLD's existing path, with `collapse_w` and `predict_w` kept as two separate weights (world/api.py:429-434).
  - The arm for any future joint gradient: an EMA target with a bounded representation term into the codec, which then needs a VICReg term on the codec latent.
- **Measured.**
  - D3, relative MSE against persistence, tones: 0.395/0.354 frozen vs 0.433/0.393 live at 40 ms; 0.712/0.702 vs 0.719/0.714 at 200 ms.

issues.what: The S0b resume rule cannot work with how the tree mints tokens. The rule says: a resume re-tokenizes the tail from run.cursor at the restored vocabulary, and if the re-measured windows_in_epoch differs from the saved value, the resume is refused. In the tree, TOK mints on its own TOK_GROW_EVERY=200 cadence (due.mint), separately from the retok act on TOK_RETOK_EVERY=3000. So by the time of a checkpoint, the saved vocabulary almost always holds mints made after the last act. Re-segmenting the tail with those mints gives a shorter tail, and the resume is refused. The 'alloc' and 'bpe' arms fail the same way, because the §11 option 'recompute the stride maps from the restored teacher' uses an EMA teacher that has moved since the last act. D1's bit-identical resume, which the judge reproduced, holds only because D1 mints and refreshes its snapshot ONLY inside act() (d1/run_arm.py:429-470, 670-682). The shipped design has neither property.
issues.evidence: Tree: loop.py:2183-2206 mints on due.mint every flush it fires, and only due.retok is deferred (:2208-2230). compose.py:2612-2659 re-segments at the SAVED vocabulary on resume. Critic run (toy, seed 0, one run): a copy of D1 patched to mint every 16 windows between acts every 48 windows (critic/d1r/run_arm.py --mint_every 16; out critic/d1r/smoke/resume_mintbetween.json). Result: re-measured 231 windows against 233 saved, a MISMATCH that the synthesis's rule refuses. Continuing anyway gives max |dloss| 0.4755 and bit_identical false. Control without between-act mints (judge smoke/resume_save10.json): 0.0, bit-identical.
issues.fix: Choose one option and write it into S0b/§11. (a) A resume IS an act: re-segment the tail at the restored vocabulary, call revise_epoch_length, stamp the shift, and replace the 'must equal, else refuse' check with 'record the revision'. Bit-identity is then promised only against an uninterrupted run that acted at the same point. (b) Checkpoint vocab.rev and the teacher state as of the last act, and have TOK segment with ids up to that rev and AUD allocate with that snapshot. That needs a TOK 'segment at rev' capability: count +1 entry point or a signature move. (c) Mint only at acts (couple TOK_GROW_EVERY to the act). This also removes the stranded-negative-row problem. Whichever is chosen, add a known-answer test: save between a mint and the next act, then resume.

issues.what:
Did-it-fire and inert-lever hygiene.
- AUD_STRIDE (spec only), AUD_RATE_TOL ('alloc' only), AUD_BPE_* and AUD_RATE_STRIDE (not read under 'alloc'/'bpe') are set-but-inert at default and need declared Gates.
- tok.retok_deferred and tok.retok_satisfied_by_roll 'lose their meaning'. Left PRESENT-0 they would read 'armed and did not fire'; they should be ABSENT with a reason.
- tok.due_dropped == 0 needs a rule for a Due raised on the final window.
- OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM ships 0, so the 'OPT shift stamp' at media arrival does not re-warm the LM. The defaults list should say so.
issues.evidence: opt/levers.py:791 lr_shift_warm = Lever(0, ...). Contract Q-RUN-8 counter semantics (docs/04_CONTRACT.md:4232-4240).
issues.fix: Add Gates for arm-only levers, retire or re-declare the deferral counters, define the final-window act, and state OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=0 in the ON/OFF list.

issues.what: The EMA teacher is ON by default with no support at LM level. In the one paired seed, online codes gave the same LM bits and better recover exact.
issues.evidence: D3 s0, ttc25 vs live25: tones 111.534 vs 112.35 bits/s, melody 131.325 vs 131.421; recover exact tones 0.231 vs 0.315, melody 0.172 vs 0.188.
issues.fix: Keep the EMA as the flip-control arm in the S3/S5 matrix, with the default decided by the pre-declared rule. Say in 0b that its measured value is flip rate, not LM bits.

issues.what: The S0b ship rule ('keep 3000 unless BOTH seeds read worse than seed noise') lets an act that hurts at one seed ship, and 'seed noise' is undefined. The cost of re-tokenizing a 17 MB tail at owner scale is unmeasured. Per-token level consumers other than FAB (the MEM surprise gate at 0.3, the CAP stall band, DOM competence) get no shift handling at text acts. The OPT horizon revision does not say it preserves LR continuity.
issues.evidence: Synthesis §13 S0b measurement row; map risks (5) and (9); archive -2.189 bits/byte from retok side effects.
issues.fix: Define noise from paired seeds, use a non-inferiority margin, time TOK.tokenize on the owner's tail, and extend the shift stamp or a documented per-byte reading to MEM, CAP and DOM.

issues.what: 'Liveness does not touch text' was measured on synthetic 15-symbol Markov byte text, with no TOK, SIG, DOM, FAB or MEM.
issues.evidence: d3/run.py markov_text alphabet 'etaoinshrdlu .,'; D1 uses the same markov_text for its text records.
issues.fix: Label the result as toy-text, and let S0b/S5 carry the real-text check.

repro.summary:
Independent reproduction, run 2026-09-25 from 14:02 to 15:01 in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/mm2/repro/. I copied code and checkpoints from d1/d2/d3; the md5 sums of the copied checkpoints match the judge's copies. Result files are in repro/{d1,d3,d2}/res/, logs in repro/logs/, and the side-by-side table (made by repro/compare.py) is in repro/compare_out.txt. Nothing in the repo or in d1/d2/d3/judge was modified. All runs used CPU with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. Compute: about 159 process-minutes over about 58 minutes of wall time, with up to 3 single-thread processes at once. That is within the ~80 min limit if it means wall time, but over it if it means CPU time.

SAME SEED: every rerun reproduced its original bit for bit, even with other processes running at the same time. D1: frozen25lat s0, live25 s0 and frozen25 s0; the aggregate.json from aggregate.py matches exactly. D3: frozen25c s0, flipdist s0, aggregate.py and drift_summary.py are identical. D1: the resume test gives max |dloss| 0.0, windows 232=232, revisions 4=4. D2: dbg_grad at w 0.1 and at w 1.0 matches line for line, and summarize.py matches. I did not rerun D3 frozen25/ttc25 s0/s1 or the judge's hot/cold s0 runs myself; the judge already reproduced ttc25c s0 exactly.

NEW SEEDS (2 and 3; D3 retrained its codec for each new seed):
- Coordinate/lattice rows (the lever the recommendation rests on) held at every new seed in both harnesses.
  - D1, frozen: A after A -12.4% / -14.2%, B at end -11.3% / -11.1%.
  - D1, live: A after A -11.6% / -13.5%, B at end -9.9% / -11.4%.
  - D3 frozen25c vs frozen25: tones -12.8% / -12.4%, melody -13.2% / -11.3%.
  - D3 ttc25c vs frozen25: bits/s -7.9% to -11.4% and mel -10.3% to -13.3%.
  - The B-understanding gain did not replicate: frozen 0.214 vs 0.226 at s2; live 0.19 vs 0.214 (s2) and 0.179 vs 0.238 (s3).
- Live vs frozen at low plasticity (D1): live beat frozen in 12/12 new-seed readings, 6 with table rows and 6 with lattice rows (-0.93 to -7.76 bits/s). All D1 seeds share one codec-phase checkpoint (codec25.pt), so codec initialisation is not varied there.
- Frame rate: the fixed stride still won.
  - ttcMR vs ttcN25: s1 +14.3% / +10.6%, s2 +3.6% / +15.2% (the adaptive arm is worse).
  - ttcMRc vs ttc25c: tones -0.5% / -1.6%, melody +5.4% / +5.5% (mixed; melody worse at all 3 seeds).
  - D1 live50bpe vs live50def at s2: +1.22, -1.69, +5.73, so BPE was worse in 7 of 9 readings over 3 seeds.
  - D2 fixed s1 beats the router s1: A mel 0.4158 vs 0.4659, melody teacher-forced mel 0.3957 vs 0.5885.
- Q-RUN-8 option (a) worked again at s2: windows 12996 -> 12096 over 6 revisions, 81,081/684,767 (11.8%) minted, 0 in the deferred control, and every assertion passed.

CAVEATS I found:
- (a) Claim 7's "one lattice step" means each changed coordinate moves one level. At 500 steps only 63-68% of flipped codes change a single coordinate.
- (b) In claim 10, at the default GMM weight 0.1 the GMM gradient norm is higher than caption CE at P2 step 99 (2.951 vs 1.621) and about equal at 149 (1.065 vs 1.058). The claim cites only step 49.
- (c) Claim 4's D1 A-mel direction flipped at s2: 0.5107, better than frozen's 0.5319.
- (d) Claim 5's cost was smaller at s2 (+3.4% / +3.2%), and band recovery fell (0.935 vs 0.963).
- (e) New D3 text readings reach 2.0579 (ttcN25 s1), outside the claimed [2.003, 2.043]. It is not forgetting, since text is still 0.40 below P0.

Not run within the budget: new seeds for D2 base/d2 (claim 10), for the codec-side allocator in drift.py, and a second new seed for ttc25 (claim 5) and for the hot/cold runs (claim 4).
